P01-S004.text: - P01-S004 FACT (current external context, not evidence of legacy runtime behaviour; read on 2026-11-26): (a) Kite Connect v3 documentation, "Historical candle data", `https://kite.trade/docs/connect/v3/historical`: each candle record is an array of timestamp, open, high, low, close and volume (OI as a seventh value only when requested); the example timestamps carry a `+0530` offset (for example `2017-12-15T09:15:00+0530`); the examples are in ascending time, but the page states no ordering rule and says nothing about adjustment for splits, bonuses or other corporate actions; it does not define `volume` (per candle or cumulative) and does not say whether the last candle of an answer can still be forming; the intervals listed are minute, day, 3minute, 5minute, 10minute, 15minute, 30minute and 60minute. (b) Python documentation "Built-in Functions", `https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html`: `float()` accepts strings for NaN and infinity; `int()` of a float "truncates towards zero"; `max()`/`min()` raise `ValueError` on an empty iterable without `default`, and with several maximal (minimal) items return "the first one encountered"; `round()` rounds half to even and notes that `round(2.675, 2)` gives `2.67`; "The built-in sorted() function is guaranteed to be stable". (c) "Built-in Types", `https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html`: "The sort() method is guaranteed to be stable"; "Dictionaries preserve insertion order" (guaranteed since 3.7) and dict views iterate in insertion order. (d) "math — Mathematical functions", `https://docs.python.org/3/library/math.html`: `log10` returns the base-10 logarithm; the CPython implementation raises `ValueError` for invalid operations such as `log(0.0)`; a NaN input generally yields NaN; the entries for `floor` and `ceil` say nothing about infinite or NaN arguments. (e) "datetime — Basic date and time types", `https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html`: a datetime is aware if its `utcoffset()` does not return `None`, otherwise naive; subtraction of a naive and an aware datetime raises `TypeError`; order comparison between naive and aware datetimes raises `TypeError`; aware operands with different `tzinfo` are subtracted as if converted to UTC; `replace(tzinfo=None)` makes a naive datetime "with no conversion of date and time data"; `timedelta.total_seconds()` returns the total seconds. P01-S039.label: FACT
P01-S039.text: - P01-S039 FACT (guard, L37 to L40): `n = len(candles)`; it returns an empty list when `left < 1`, `right < 1` or `n < (left + right + 1)`. No other input is checked: not the types of `left` and `right`, not the candle values, not the order or uniqueness of the bars.

P01-S040.label: FACT
P01-S040.text: - P01-S040 FACT (the scan, L42 to L45): for each index `i` in `range(left, n - right)`, `window = candles[i - left : i + right + 1]` (the `left + right + 1` bars from `i - left` to `i + right`, the candidate included) and `others` is the window without the element at position `left` of the window (the test `(i - left + j) != i`, L45, excludes exactly the candidate's own position, by index, not by identity or value). INTERPRETATION: the first `left` bars and the last `right` bars are never examined, as SR-P2 states (L14 to L15: "The first `left` and last `right` bars can never be pivots (no full window) — they are skipped").

P01-S041.label: FACT
P01-S041.text: - P01-S041 FACT (swing HIGH, L47 to L49): a HIGH pivot is appended when `all(c.high >= w.high for w in window)` and `any(c.high > w.high for w in others)`, with `Pivot(price=c.high, ts=c.ts, kind="HIGH", bar_index=i)`. FACT (swing LOW, L51 to L53): the mirror, `all(c.low <= w.low for w in window)` and `any(c.low < w.low for w in others)`, appending `Pivot(price=c.low, ts=c.ts, kind="LOW", bar_index=i)`. The comparison is non-strict against the whole window and strict against at least one other bar, as SR-P1 states (L10 to L13: "high[i] >= every high in the window [i-left, i+right] AND strictly greater than at least one neighbour in the window (so a perfectly flat plateau does not mark every bar)"). Only `high` and `low` are read; `open`, `close`, `volume` and `ts` (except as the pivot's label) play no part.

P01-S042.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S042.text: - P01-S042 INTERPRETATION (ties and plateaus; from L48 and L52): a bar that equals the window's maximum high and has at least one strictly lower neighbour in its window is a HIGH pivot even when another bar in the same window has the same high. So a plateau of two or more equal highs with lower bars around it yields one HIGH pivot for every bar of the plateau whose window contains a lower bar, all at the same price; only a window in which every high is equal yields none. Example (left = right = 2): highs `[1, 2, 5, 5, 2, 1]` give HIGH pivots at indices 2 and 3, both at 5. The same holds for LOW pivots. SR-P1's parenthesis ("a perfectly flat plateau does not mark every bar") is met only for a perfectly flat window; the test `tests/unit/test_sr_detector_units.py` L43 to L45 states the expectation for a fully flat series (nine equal bars, no pivots) only.

P01-S043.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S043.text: - P01-S043 INTERPRETATION (one bar as both HIGH and LOW; from L48 and L52): a bar whose high is the window's maximum and whose low is the window's minimum, each strictly beyond at least one other bar (an outside bar that engulfs its window), yields both a HIGH and a LOW pivot, the HIGH first (L48 before L52). The docstring's "only in degenerate single-bar windows" (L34 to L35) does not describe this case, and a single-bar window cannot occur because `left` and `right` are at least 1 (L39).

P01-S044.label: FACT
P01-S044.text: - P01-S044 FACT (output order and content): pivots are appended in increasing `i`, HIGH before LOW at the same `i` (L42 to L53); `bar_index` is the position in the given list, not a time; `ts` is the candle's `ts` unchanged. The function returns a new list and does not modify `candles`.

P01-S045.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P01-S045.text: - P01-S045 FACT and INTERPRETATION (input order): the function does not sort and does not read `ts` to order bars (L37 to L55); it treats list position as time. INTERPRETATION: (a) with `left == right` (every non-test caller passes the same `n` for both, section 8) the window is symmetric, so a list given in reverse chronological order yields the same set of pivot bars, with the same prices and `ts`, but in reversed bar order (at a bar that is both a HIGH and a LOW pivot the HIGH still comes first) and with `bar_index` counted from the newest bar; which bars are "the first `left`" and "the last `right`" then swaps, so the newest `left` bars and the oldest `right` bars are skipped. (b) A list in any other order (shuffled, or two series concatenated) yields pivots from positional neighbours that are not time neighbours, with no error. (c) A consumer that reads the output order as time (for example the most recent pivot as the last element) gets the oldest pivot from a reversed list (section 8, `regime/engine.py` L195 to L200).

P01-S046.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S046.text: - P01-S046 INTERPRETATION (duplicate and missing bars; from L44 to L53): a bar repeated consecutively (the same row twice) forms a two-bar plateau, so if the bar was a pivot strictly beyond every other bar of its window, both copies become pivots at the same price and `ts` (each copy's window holds only bars of the original window and the other copy; P01-S042), and the zone built from them counts two touches (section 5). A missing bar (a gap in the series) is not detected: the window counts list elements, not time, so the window spans more time than `left + right + 1` intervals.

P01-S047.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S047.text: - P01-S047 INTERPRETATION (numeric edge cases; Python semantics, P01-S005): a NaN `high` makes `c.high >= w.high` false for its own bar and for every bar whose window contains it (any comparison with NaN is false), so no HIGH pivot is found in any window that contains a NaN high; the same holds for NaN lows. An infinite high can be a HIGH pivot with price `inf`. Zero or negative prices are compared like any other numbers. No exception is raised for these values. A non-integer `left` or `right` would raise `TypeError` in `range` or in the slice (P01-S133); every non-test caller passes an `int` (section 8): the regime engine and the V3 runners cast with `int()` (`regime/engine.py` L193; `v3_chain/runner.py` L202; `v3_chain/pb01_runner.py` L149), and the zone builder passes `knobs.default_pivot_n`, cast with `int()` (`sr_detector/zone_builder.py` L43), or a value of `pivot_n_by_tf`, which `build_zone_knobs` copies without a cast (L44) and the loader declares as `dict[str, int]` (`core/config_loader.py` L1169).

P01-S048.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S048.text: - P01-S048 INTERPRETATION (lag of the most recent structure; from L42 and SR-P2): because the last `right` bars are never examined, the most recent bar that can be a pivot is `right` bars before the last bar given. With the committed `default_pivot_n: 5` (`config/system_config.yaml` L513; `pivot_n_by_tf` not set in the file, loader default empty, `core/config_loader.py` L1169) this is five bars: about a trading week on the daily series, and five 60-minute or five 30-minute bars on the intraday series, which can reach back across the overnight break (committed value only; the deployed value is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED, Document 06, section 4.2). If the last bar given is still forming, it can serve as a right-hand neighbour but cannot itself be a pivot; whether the broker's answers included a forming last candle is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 AUDIT HA-04).

P01-S049.label: FACT
P01-S049.text: - P01-S049 FACT (cost, failure, side effects): the function makes `n - left - right` window slices of `left + right + 1` bars each; it catches no exception, logs nothing and reads no clock or configuration.

P01-S050.label: FACT
P01-S050.text: - P01-S050 FACT (signature, L28 to L42): `cluster_zones(pivots: List[Pivot], *, cluster_pct: float, timeframe: str) -> List[Zone]`; `cluster_pct` and `timeframe` are keyword-only and have no default. Docstring: "pivots from one timeframe (mixed HIGH/LOW ok)"; "cluster_pct: a pivot joins the running cluster while its price is within this percent of the cluster's current band-high (e.g. 0.5 = 0.5%)"; "timeframe: label stamped on each produced Zone."

P01-S051.label: FACT
P01-S051.text: - P01-S051 FACT (per kind, L44 to L49): the loop takes `("HIGH", "RESISTANCE")` first and `("LOW", "SUPPORT")` second; for each it selects the pivots whose `kind` equals the pivot kind and sorts them by `price` ascending (`sorted(..., key=lambda p: p.price)`, L45 to L47); if there are none, the kind is skipped. A pivot whose `kind` is neither `"HIGH"` nor `"LOW"` is ignored without a log. INTERPRETATION (P01-S004 (b)): the sort is stable, so pivots of equal price keep their input order; that order does not affect the band, the touch count or the latest touch.

P01-S052.label: FACT
P01-S052.text: - P01-S052 FACT (the greedy pass, L51 to L60): the running cluster starts as the lowest pivot; for each following pivot `p`, `band_high = max(x.price for x in cluster)`, `tol = band_high * (cluster_pct / 100.0)`, and `p` joins the cluster if `p.price <= band_high + tol`; otherwise the cluster is closed into a zone (`_zone_from_cluster`) and a new cluster starts with `p`. After the loop the last cluster is closed (L60). Output: all RESISTANCE zones in ascending price, then all SUPPORT zones in ascending price.

P01-S053.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S053.text: - P01-S053 INTERPRETATION (the tolerance and chaining; from L52 to L56): the tolerance is a percentage of price (not an absolute amount and not ATR-based). Because the pivots are sorted ascending, `band_high` is always the price of the previous pivot, so the rule is: a pivot joins when its distance above the previous pivot is at most `cluster_pct` per cent of the previous pivot's price. Membership is therefore chained (single linkage): a zone can grow without limit while each consecutive step is within the tolerance. Example (`cluster_pct` 0.5): pivots at 100.0, 100.4, 100.8, 101.2, 101.6 and 102.0 (each step 0.4, below the tolerance of about 0.5) form one zone from 100.0 to 102.0 (2 per cent wide), although its ends are about four tolerances apart. No maximum band width exists. This is what SR-Z1 (L11 to L13) states: "a pivot joins the running cluster while it is within `cluster_pct` of the cluster's current high". The test `tests/unit/test_sr_detector_units.py` L55 to L67 states the expectation for 100.0, 100.2, 100.4 (one zone, three touches) and 105.0 (a separate zone).

P01-S054.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S054.text: - P01-S054 INTERPRETATION (minimum touches and zero-width zones; from L51 to L60): there is no minimum number of touches: a lone pivot becomes a zone with `touches = 1` and `band_low == band_high`, a band of zero width. The `Zone` docstring's "A price BAND (never a single line)" (`models.py` L62) is not enforced by the code: a zone can be a single price, and so can a cluster of pivots at one price. The stored band is never widened in the four files; only the two membership checks that apply a buffer widen it, for that check only: `contains` with a positive `buffer_pct` (P01-S024, P01-S027) and `_level_in_band` with `band_buffer_pct` (P01-S083). The round-number test applies none (P01-S084).

P01-S055.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S055.text: - P01-S055 INTERPRETATION (parameter edge cases; from L54 to L55): `cluster_pct = 0` joins only pivots of exactly equal price; a negative `cluster_pct` makes even equal positive prices form separate zones; neither is rejected (the function checks nothing; `SRDetectorConfig.cluster_pct` is a plain `float`, `core/config_loader.py` L1171, with no validator among those at L1225 to L1255). The committed value is `cluster_pct: 0.5` (`config/system_config.yaml` L514), equal to the loader default (L1171) and to the `build_zone_knobs` fallback (`sr_detector/zone_builder.py` L45); the deployed value is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (Document 06, section 4.2). NaN pivot prices cannot come from `find_swing_pivots` (P01-S047); a `+inf` HIGH pivot would form a zone of its own at the top of the RESISTANCE list, and a `-inf` LOW pivot one at the bottom of the SUPPORT list (the join test `p.price <= band_high + tol` fails against an infinite neighbour; P01-S133).

P01-S056.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S056.text: - P01-S056 INTERPRETATION (what a touch is; from L72 and P01-S042, P01-S046): `touches` counts pivots, not distinct swings, bars or days. A plateau of equal extremes (P01-S042) or a duplicated bar (P01-S046) yields several pivots at one price, all in one zone, so the touch count can exceed the number of separate swings. A bar that is both a HIGH and a LOW pivot (P01-S043) adds one touch to a RESISTANCE zone and one to a SUPPORT zone.

P01-S057.label: FACT
P01-S057.text: - P01-S057 FACT (L65 to L75): `prices = [p.price for p in cluster]`; `last_ts = max((p.ts for p in cluster), default=None)`; it returns `Zone(band_low=min(prices), band_high=max(prices), kind=kind, touches=len(cluster), timeframe=timeframe, last_touch_ts=last_ts)`. This matches SR-Z2 (L14 to L15): "Zone band = [min, max] of the cluster's pivot prices. touches = count of pivots; last_touch_ts = most recent pivot ts (recency)."

P01-S058.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S058.text: - P01-S058 INTERPRETATION (time fields; from L67 and P01-S004 (e)): the only time kept is the latest pivot `ts`; the earliest touch, the list of touch times and the bar indices are not kept, and the `Zone` does not keep its pivots. The cluster is never empty when this helper is called (L51, L59), so `default=None` is not reached from `cluster_zones`. `max` over the `ts` values uses order comparisons, so a cluster that mixes naive and aware `datetime` values, or holds a `None` `ts` beside a `datetime`, raises `TypeError` (a single-pivot cluster returns its one value without a comparison). Within one fetched series the `ts` values come from one parser (P01-S016), so a mix is not expected from the main path (INTERPRETATION). `ts` is the candle's label; A05's records read the broker's label as the start of the interval (A05 RECONCILED TOPIC RECORD section 4.5, L130), so the latest touch is dated at the start of the bar that made the extreme, not at the moment the extreme printed.

P01-S059.label: FACT
P01-S059.text: - P01-S059 FACT (signature, L78 to L90): `volume_profile_nodes(candles: List[Candle], *, bins: int = 24, node_frac: float = 0.7) -> List[float]`. Docstring: "Return the centre prices of high-volume price bins (volume nodes, SR-Z4). A crude volume-by-price: bucket each bar's volume at its mid price across `bins` equal-width buckets over [min low, max high]; a node is any bucket whose total volume >= node_frac * (max bucket volume)."

P01-S060.label: FACT
P01-S060.text: - P01-S060 FACT (guards, L91 to L96): it returns an empty list when `candles` is empty or `bins < 1`; it computes `lo = min(c.low for c in candles)` and `hi = max(c.high for c in candles)` and returns an empty list when `hi <= lo`.

P01-S061.label: FACT
P01-S061.text: - P01-S061 FACT (binning, L98 to L107): `width = (hi - lo) / bins`; `buckets = [0.0] * bins`; for each candle, `mid = (c.high + c.low) / 2.0`, `idx = int((mid - lo) / width)`, set to `bins - 1` if `idx >= bins` and to 0 if `idx < 0`, then `buckets[idx] += float(c.volume)`.

P01-S062.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S062.text: - P01-S062 INTERPRETATION (what the binning means; from L98 to L107): the buckets are equal in price width, `(max high − min low) / bins`, so their width scales with the range of the window, not with the price level. Each bar's whole volume goes to the one bucket that contains its mid-range price `(high + low) / 2`; it is not spread over the bar's range and does not use the close or a typical price. `int()` truncates toward zero (P01-S004 (b)), so `idx` is the bucket whose lower edge is at or below `mid`. For valid bars `mid` lies within `[lo, hi]`, so the clamps (L103 to L106) act when `mid` is at `hi` (a zero-range bar at the window's top, `idx == bins`) or, through floating-point rounding, a hair below it (P01-S133; at `mid == hi` the rounded index can also come out as `bins - 1` with no clamp needed), and for an invalid bar with `high < low` whose mid falls outside the range.

P01-S063.label: FACT
P01-S063.text: - P01-S063 FACT (nodes, L109 to L116): `peak = max(buckets)`; if `peak <= 0` it returns an empty list; otherwise it returns `lo + (i + 0.5) * width` for every bucket `i` with `v >= node_frac * peak`, in ascending price order. INTERPRETATION: the nodes are bucket centres, not traded prices; adjacent node buckets are not merged; the number of nodes is not limited; a series with zero volume everywhere (for example volumes defaulted to 0 by `from_kite`, P01-S018) gives no nodes.

P01-S064.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S064.text: - P01-S064 INTERPRETATION (parameter and value edge cases; from L91 to L116, P01-S005): `node_frac <= 0` makes every bucket a node, empty ones included (`v >= 0` holds), and `node_frac > 1` makes none; neither is rejected (`volume_node_frac` is a plain `float`, `core/config_loader.py` L1176). A non-integer `bins` raises `TypeError` at `[0.0] * bins`. A negative volume reduces its bucket. A NaN high or low in any candle, a `+inf` high or a `-inf` low leads to `int()` of a NaN at L102 (directly, or through a NaN or infinite `width`, `inf / inf` being NaN), which raises `ValueError` (P01-S005, P01-S133); an infinity on the wrong side of an invalid bar (a `+inf` low or a `-inf` high beside finite candles) leads to `int()` of an infinity, which raises `OverflowError`, and a lone such candle gives `hi <= lo` and an empty list. The function catches nothing. A NaN volume makes its bucket NaN, which never satisfies `v >= node_frac * peak`; whether it becomes `peak` depends on its position, because `max` keeps a NaN only when it is the first item (P01-S133): a NaN in bucket 0 makes `peak` NaN, `peak <= 0` false and every node test false, so no node is returned; a NaN in a later bucket is passed over. (A `Candle` made by `from_kite` cannot carry a NaN volume, P01-S018.)

P01-S065.text: - P01-S065 FACT (committed values and fallbacks): `config/system_config.yaml` L508 to L545 has no `volume_bins` or `volume_node_frac` key, so the loader defaults apply (`volume_bins: int = 24`, `volume_node_frac: float = 0.7`, `core/config_loader.py` L1175 to L1176), equal to the `build_zone_knobs` fallbacks (`sr_detector/zone_builder.py` L46 to L47) and the function defaults (L81 to L82). P01-S070.label: FACT
P01-S070.text: - P01-S070 FACT (`score_zones`, L62 to L73): signature `score_zones(zones_by_tf: Dict[str, List[Zone]], ctx: ConfluenceContext, params: ScoringParams) -> List[ScoredZone]`; docstring "Merge across TFs and score each merged zone. RESISTANCE + SUPPORT separately." For `kind` in `("RESISTANCE", "SUPPORT")` it calls `_merge_across_tfs(zones_by_tf, kind, params.merge_pct)` and appends `_score_group(group, kind, ctx, params)` for every group. Output order: all RESISTANCE groups, then all SUPPORT groups, each in the order the merge produced (ascending centre, P01-S072). Nothing is filtered out: every group is returned, LOW ones included, and nothing is sorted by score. An empty `zones_by_tf` gives an empty list. A `Zone` whose `kind` is neither value is dropped without a log (L86).

P01-S071.label: FACT
P01-S071.text: - P01-S071 FACT (`_merge_across_tfs`, L80 to L101): it flattens the zones of the given kind from every timeframe in the iteration order of `zones_by_tf.values()` (L84 to L86), sorts them by `center` ascending (`flat.sort(key=lambda z: z.center)`, L87), and builds groups greedily: the first zone starts a group; each next zone `z` is compared with the current (last) group's mean centre `cur_center = sum(x.center for x in cur) / len(cur)` (L95), with `tol = cur_center * (merge_pct / 100.0)` (L96); if `abs(z.center - cur_center) <= tol` it joins the group, otherwise it starts a new one (L97 to L100). Docstring: "Greedy-cluster same-kind zones from all TFs by centre proximity."

P01-S072.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S072.text: - P01-S072 INTERPRETATION (the merge rule; from L84 to L100 and P01-S004 (b), (c)): (a) the tolerance is a percentage of the group's running mean centre, unweighted by touches or width, and is compared with the distance between centres, not between band edges, so two overlapping bands with distant centres can stay apart and two disjoint bands with close centres can merge; (b) because the zones are sorted ascending, the mean drifts upward as members join, so a group can extend beyond `merge_pct` of its lowest member (a milder form of the chaining of P01-S053); (c) the rule does not require the members to come from different timeframes: two zones of the same timeframe join one group when the second falls within the tolerance of the group's mean, which can happen through a zone of another timeframe between them. Example with the committed values (`cluster_pct` 0.5, `merge_pct` 0.4): daily single-pivot zones at 100.0 and 100.55 stay separate in `cluster_zones` (100.55 is above 100.0 + 0.5); a 60-minute zone at 100.35 joins the 100.0 zone (distance 0.35, tolerance 0.4), the group mean becomes 100.175, and the 100.55 zone joins too (distance 0.375, tolerance about 0.4007), giving one group with two daily zones and one 60-minute zone, `timeframes` of length 2; (d) the sort is stable and `dict` iteration follows insertion order, so zones with equal centres keep the timeframe order of `zones_by_tf` (on the configured path, the order of the fetched series); with equal centres this order does not change the groups.

P01-S073.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S073.text: - P01-S073 INTERPRETATION (parameter edge cases): `merge_pct = 0` merges only zones with exactly equal centres; a negative `merge_pct` or a negative mean centre makes the tolerance negative, so nothing merges (an `abs` value is never below a negative number); a mean centre of exactly 0 gives a tolerance of 0, so only a zone whose centre is also 0 joins; a zone with an infinite centre (from an infinite pivot, P01-S055) never joins a group, `abs(inf - inf)` being NaN (P01-S133); NaN centres cannot arise from zones built by `cluster_zones` from `find_swing_pivots` output (P01-S047, P01-S055).

P01-S074.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P01-S074.text: - P01-S074 FACT and INTERPRETATION (SR-C1 against the code): SR-C1 (L11 to L12) reads "Merge same-kind zones ACROSS timeframes by centre proximity (within merge_pct) into one band; the merged band spans the union." FACT: the merged band is the union `[min band_low, max band_high]` (`_score_group` L107 to L108), so a gap between members is inside the merged band. INTERPRETATION: "ACROSS timeframes" describes the purpose; the code also merges zones of one timeframe (P01-S072 (c)); "within merge_pct" is measured from the group's mean centre, not pairwise.

P01-S075.label: FACT
P01-S075.text: - P01-S075 FACT (group summary, L107 to L114): `band_low = min(z.band_low for z in group)`; `band_high = max(z.band_high for z in group)`; `timeframes = tuple(sorted({z.timeframe for z in group}))` (distinct labels, sorted as strings, so `"30minute" < "60minute" < "day"`); `total_touches = sum(z.touches for z in group)`; `last_touch = max((z.last_touch_ts for z in group if z.last_touch_ts is not None), default=None)`.

P01-S076.label: FACT

P01-S077.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P01-S077.text:
- P01-S077 FACT and INTERPRETATION (formula): the score is
  `score = w_swing·min(T, touch_cap) + w_multi_tf·N_tf + w_volume·[volume node in band ± buffer] + w_prior_day·[PDH, PDL or PDC in band ± buffer] + w_round·[round number in band] + w_recency·r`
  where `T` is the summed touches of the group, `N_tf` the number of distinct timeframe labels, `[...]` is 1 when the test holds and 0 otherwise, and `r` the recency factor of section 6.5. Each external vote counts once, however many levels or nodes fall in the band. INTERPRETATION (arithmetic on the committed values, P01-S069): with the three committed timeframes (`config/system_config.yaml` L510) the score of a group lies between 2 (one touch, one timeframe, no other vote) and 10 (4 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 0.5 + 0.5).

P01-S078.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S078.text: - P01-S078 INTERPRETATION ("distinct method-types"; from L119 to L126 and L146): for any group (each zone has at least one touch, P01-S054) with `w_swing > 0`, `w_multi_tf > 0` and `touch_cap >= 1`, both `swing_pivots` and `multi_tf` are always appended, so `distinct_types` is always at least 2. With the committed weights and the loader's `touch_cap` of 4 (not in the YAML, P01-S069) the condition "≥2 distinct method-types" of SR-C3 is therefore always met, and the HIGH test reduces to `score >= t_high` and at least two timeframes. `multi_tf` is appended for a single-timeframe group too (`1.0 × 1`), so it counts as a method even when no second timeframe agrees.

P01-S079.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S079.text: - P01-S079 INTERPRETATION (what reaches each bucket with the committed values; from P01-S076 to P01-S078, P01-S080): (a) every group that has zones from all three configured timeframes has `swing >= 3` and `multi = 3`, so `score >= 6` and it is HIGH without any volume, prior-day, round-number or recency vote; (b) a two-timeframe group is HIGH when its summed touches are at least 3 (swing ≥ 3 + multi 2 = 5), or with two touches plus one volume or prior-day vote, or with two touches plus the round-number vote and a full recency factor of 1.0; (c) a single-timeframe group can never be HIGH, whatever its score (up to 8); it is MEDIUM from two touches (2 + 1 = 3), or from one touch plus one volume or prior-day vote; (d) a single pivot on one timeframe with no other vote scores 2 (LOW), or 2.5 with a round number or up to 2.5 with recency, reaching MEDIUM only with both and `r = 1.0`. The test `tests/unit/test_sr_detector_units.py` L83 to L95 states the expectation that two zones with five and three touches on two timeframes, with no external evidence, are HIGH with `swing_pivots` and `multi_tf` as their evidence; L104 to L108 that four touches on one timeframe are MEDIUM, "only 1 TF -> cannot be HIGH"; L98 to L101 that one touch on one timeframe is LOW.

P01-S080.label: FACT
P01-S080.text: - P01-S080 FACT (`_bucket`, L162 to L167): returns `"HIGH"` if `score >= p.t_high and distinct_types >= 2 and num_tfs >= 2`; else `"MEDIUM"` if `score >= p.t_med`; else `"LOW"`. Both thresholds are inclusive. Nothing checks that `t_high >= t_med`.

P01-S081.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S081.text: - P01-S081 INTERPRETATION (zero or negative weights; from L120, L125, L129 to L138, L142): the swing, multi-timeframe and recency votes are appended only when positive, but the volume, prior-day and round-number votes are appended whenever their test holds, whatever their weight. A weight of 0 for one of these three would still add an evidence entry (contribution 0) and count it in `distinct_types`; a negative weight would lower the score. The committed weights are all positive (P01-S069), so this is latent on the committed path.

P01-S082.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S082.text: - P01-S082 INTERPRETATION (floating point and rounding): the score is a sum of floats and is compared with the thresholds without rounding; the recency contribution is a continuous value, so a score can sit just below a threshold by a fraction. `ScoredZone.to_dict` rounds the score to four decimals for storage (P01-S028); the bucket is decided on the unrounded value.

P01-S083.label: FACT
P01-S083.text: - P01-S083 FACT (`_level_in_band`, L170 to L177): returns `False` for an empty `levels`; otherwise `center = (low + high) / 2.0`, `pad = center * (buffer_pct / 100.0)`, and returns `any((low - pad) <= lv <= (high + pad) for lv in levels)`. INTERPRETATION: the same inclusive, centre-relative percentage buffer as `Zone.contains` (P01-S024), applied to the merged union band; with the committed `band_buffer_pct: 0.1` the band is widened by 0.1 per cent of its centre on each side. A NaN level never matches.

P01-S084.label: FACT
P01-S084.text: - P01-S084 FACT (`_has_round_number`, L180 to L192): docstring "A multiple of the price magnitude (or half-magnitude) falling in the band." It computes `center = (low + high) / 2.0`; returns `False` if `center <= 0`; sets `magnitude = 10.0 ** math.floor(math.log10(center))` (comment "e.g. 523 -> 100"); for `step` in `(magnitude, magnitude / 2.0)` (skipping a non-positive step) it computes `k = math.ceil(low / step - 1e-9)` and returns `True` if `k * step <= high + 1e-9`; otherwise `False`. No buffer is applied.

P01-S085.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S085.text: - P01-S085 INTERPRETATION (the round-number rule; from L185 to L191): (a) `k * step` is the smallest multiple of `step` at or above `low` (the `- 1e-9` lets a `low` a hair above a multiple, in units of the step, count as that multiple), and the test asks whether it lies at or below `high` (with an absolute `1e-9` allowance): that is, whether the band contains a multiple of the step. (b) Every multiple of `magnitude` is also a multiple of `magnitude / 2`, so the first step adds nothing (apart from a band whose `low` lies within the `1e-9` allowance, in units of the step, above a multiple of `magnitude`): the rule is in effect "the band contains a multiple of half the power of ten below its centre". (c) The step depends on the decade of the centre: for a centre from 100 to just under 1,000 the step is 50; from 1,000 to just under 10,000 it is 500; from 10 to just under 100 it is 5. Relative to price the step therefore ranges from 50 per cent (centre at a power of ten) down to just over 5 per cent (centre just under the next power of ten), and it jumps tenfold when the centre crosses a power of ten (a band centred at 99.9 tests multiples of 5; one centred at 100.1 tests multiples of 50). (d) A zero-width band (`low == high`, P01-S054) matches only when its single price is a multiple of the step within the tolerances. (e) Example: a band 498 to 502 (centre 500, step 50) matches at 500; a band 520 to 521 (centre 520.5) does not, the next multiple of 50 above 520 being 550.

P01-S086.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S086.text: - P01-S086 INTERPRETATION (edge cases; P01-S005): a non-positive centre returns `False`; a NaN centre passes the `center <= 0` test (it is false), `math.log10` returns NaN and `math.floor` of NaN raises `ValueError`; a `+inf` centre gives `math.log10(inf) = inf` and `math.floor(inf)` raises `OverflowError` (a `-inf` centre is non-positive and returns `False`). Neither exception is caught in the function or in `_score_group`. NaN or infinite bands cannot come from pivots produced by `find_swing_pivots` except through an infinite pivot price (P01-S047, P01-S055): a `+inf` HIGH pivot gives a `+inf` centre and so the `OverflowError`; a `-inf` LOW pivot gives `False`.

P01-S087.label: FACT
P01-S087.text: - P01-S087 FACT (a second round-number rule in the package, cross-reference only): `sr_detector/zone_builder.py` L124 to L140 (`round_number_levels`, the zone-builder part's) uses the same magnitude and half-magnitude steps to list the round levels just below and above a price (rounded to six decimals), for the anchor payload. It is not called by the four files; `_has_round_number` does not use it.

P01-S088.label: FACT
P01-S088.text: - P01-S088 FACT (`_recency_factor`, L195 to L211): returns `0.0` if `last_touch is None`; sets `now = ctx.now` and returns `1.0` if `now is None`; if exactly one of `now` and `last_touch` is naive (`(now.tzinfo is None) != (last_touch.tzinfo is None)`), it replaces the `tzinfo` of both with `None` (comment L203: "tz-safety: kite candle ts may be aware (IST) while now_fn() differs."); computes `age_days = (now - last_touch).total_seconds() / 86400.0`; returns `1.0` if `ctx.recency_window_days <= 0`; otherwise `factor = 1.0 - (age_days / ctx.recency_window_days)` and returns `max(p.recency_min_factor, min(1.0, factor))`.

P01-S089.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S089.text: - P01-S089 INTERPRETATION (what the factor measures; from L207 to L211 and P01-S004 (e)): (a) the decay is linear in calendar time (seconds divided by 86,400), counting weekends, holidays and overnight hours, not trading days or bars: a touch `w` days old gets `1 − w/90` with the default window, reaching 0 at 90 days; (b) the factor is clamped to at most 1.0, so a `last_touch` later than `now` (for example a bar label in the future relative to an `as_of` clock) gets the full factor; (c) the lower clamp is `recency_min_factor` (0.0 committed through the loader default), so a touch older than the window gives 0.0 and no `recency` entry (L142); a `recency_min_factor` above 0 would give every dated zone a recency vote, and one above 1 would return that value, above the upper clamp (no validation, P01-S069); (d) `last_touch` is the latest pivot's bar label (P01-S058), and pivots are never closer to the end of the series than `right` bars (P01-S048), so the most recent possible touch is several bars old; with the committed values a daily touch seven calendar days old gives `r ≈ 0.922` and a contribution of about 0.461.

P01-S090.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S090.text: - P01-S090 INTERPRETATION (time-zone handling; from L203 to L207 and P01-S004 (e)): when one side is aware and the other naive, both are reduced to their wall-clock digits; the age equals the elapsed time only if the aware value's wall clock is in the same zone as the naive value's (both IST, as the `Candle` docstring and the comment assume). When both are aware with different `tzinfo`, Python subtracts them as UTC instants, which gives the elapsed time between the two instants. When both are naive, the age is the wall-clock difference. No case raises for values whose `tzinfo`, where present, returns an offset (as a fixed `+0530` offset and the `timezone` of `core/time_authority.py` L59 do); Python counts a value whose `tzinfo` returns no offset as naive (P01-S004 (e)), which the L204 test, based on `tzinfo is None`, would treat as aware, so such a value beside an aware one would make the subtraction raise `TypeError`; no producer of such a `tzinfo` was found in the callers of section 8.

P01-S091.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S091.text: - P01-S091 INTERPRETATION (full credit when no clock is given; from L200 to L202 and L208 to L209): a `None` `now` or a non-positive window gives every dated zone `r = 1.0`, the maximum recency vote, rather than none. The function does not read a clock itself (P01-S010); the time base is whatever the caller places in `ConfluenceContext.now` (section 8: the detector's and warmer's `_safe_now()`, which return `None` if the clock function raises, `sr_detector/detector.py` L305 to L309, `sr_detector/zone_warmer.py` L146 to L150, `v3_chain/watchlist_capture.py` L232 to L236; the V3 runners' `as_of`).

P01-S092.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S092.text: - P01-S092 INTERPRETATION (determinism; from P01-S010 and P01-S004 (b), (c)): the four files are deterministic functions of their inputs: no clock, no randomness, no global state; sorts are stable and `dict` iteration follows insertion order. The same candles, parameters and `now` give the same zones, scores, buckets and output order. The output depends on input order only through the pivot positions (P01-S045). The timeframe order of `zones_by_tf` decides only the order of members inside a group for zones with equal centres, which changes no field of the `ScoredZone` (P01-S072 (d)) except, at most, which of two equal `last_touch_ts` values is the object kept.

P01-S093.label: FACT
P01-S093.text: - P01-S093 FACT (output order and its consumers, interface only): `score_zones` returns zones by kind and ascending centre, not by score or by distance to any price (P01-S070). `sr_detector/detector.py` L253 to L254 logs `[z.to_dict() for z in scored if z.kind == ...][: self._max_zones_logged]` for each kind (`max_zones_logged` not in the YAML; loader default 12, `core/config_loader.py` L1197). INTERPRETATION: when there are more than that many zones of one kind, the ones kept in the log are the lowest-priced, not the strongest or the nearest; the slicing is the detector's logic and is recorded here only because it depends on this order (owned by the part that studies `detector.py`). Consumers that choose a zone by price select by their own key (`min`/`max` on centre or band edge: `sr_detector/flags.py` L122, L133, L135; `screening/retest_monitor.py` L390; `orders/structure_exit_manager.py` L270, L277; `v3_chain/watchlist_capture.py` L214), so they do not depend on the order except for ties, where `min`/`max` return the first item encountered (P01-S004 (b)).

P01-S094.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S094.text: - P01-S094 INTERPRETATION (input order; from P01-S021, P01-S045, P01-S051, P01-S058, P01-S061, P01-S071): nothing in the chain from `Candle.from_kite` to `score_zones` orders candles by time. Only `find_swing_pivots` depends on candle order, and it uses list position as time. `cluster_zones` and `_merge_across_tfs` re-sort by price and by centre, `_zone_from_cluster` and `_score_group` take the latest `ts` with `max`, and `volume_profile_nodes` sums per bucket, so none of these depends on order. Consequences: (a) a series in descending time gives the same zones as the same series ascending, and the same scores for the same `ConfluenceContext`, because every caller uses equal `left` and `right` (P01-S045 (a)); the context's prior-day levels are not the same (next sentence); (b) a series in any other order gives pivots from non-neighbouring bars and therefore different zones, with no error; (c) a consumer that reads the pivot list's order as time is affected even by a descending series (P01-S045 (c); `regime/engine.py` L195 to L200, A18's; the V3 runners' `gate_htf` inputs, P01-S135). Outside the four files, `prior_day_levels` (`sr_detector/zone_builder.py` L78 to L82) takes `daily[-2]` as the prior day, which assumes ascending order (the zone-builder part's logic). Whether the server's rows ever arrived out of order is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 AUDIT CM-05).

P01-S095.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S095.text: - P01-S095 INTERPRETATION (duplicates and gaps; from P01-S046, P01-S056, P01-S061): a duplicated bar can create two pivots at one price and time and so two touches, which raises the swing vote (up to `touch_cap`) and can lift a zone's bucket (P01-S079); its volume is counted twice in its price bucket. A gap (missing bars) is not detected anywhere in the four files; a pivot window then spans more time than its bar count suggests. No function de-duplicates by `ts`.

P01-S096.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S096.text: - P01-S096 INTERPRETATION (a still-forming last bar; from P01-S048, P01-S062): a forming last bar cannot be a pivot (it is among the last `right` bars) but its high and low can decide whether the bars before it are pivots, and its partial volume enters the volume profile at its current mid. Whether the broker's answers included such a bar is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 AUDIT HA-04).

P01-S097.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P01-S097.text: - P01-S097 FACT and INTERPRETATION (bad values, by function): `from_kite` raises on a missing key, a `None` price or a non-numeric string, accepts NaN and infinity, and turns a missing or `None` volume into 0 (P01-S017, P01-S018); `find_swing_pivots` silently finds no pivot in any window containing a NaN and can emit an infinite pivot (P01-S047); `cluster_zones` and `_merge_across_tfs` raise nothing for finite or infinite prices (P01-S055, P01-S073); `volume_profile_nodes` raises `ValueError` for a NaN high or low, a `+inf` high or a `-inf` low, and `OverflowError` for an infinity on the wrong side of an invalid bar (P01-S064); `_has_round_number` raises `ValueError` for a NaN band centre and `OverflowError` for a `+inf` one (P01-S086); a mix of naive and aware `ts` values raises `TypeError` in `_zone_from_cluster` or `_score_group` (P01-S058, P01-S075) but not in `_recency_factor` (P01-S090). None of the four files checks `high >= low`, positive prices or non-negative volume, and none catches an exception. Where an exception goes is the callers' logic (section 8). Whether any such value reached the code in production is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 AUDIT CM-10).
P01-S097.sec: 7. Input-order, data-quality and numeric edge cases across the four files (summary)

P01-S098.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S098.text: - P01-S098 INTERPRETATION (zero and negative prices; from P01-S024, P01-S055, P01-S073, P01-S084): no function rejects a zero or negative price. The percentage tolerances and buffers are multiples of a price, so they are zero at a zero price and negative at a negative one: for negative prices `contains` and `_level_in_band` narrow the band, `cluster_zones` stops joining equal prices and `_merge_across_tfs` merges nothing; at a zero price the buffer and tolerances are zero, so equal prices still join and merge; `_has_round_number` returns `False` for both.
P01-S098.sec: 7. Input-order, data-quality and numeric edge cases across the four files (summary)

P01-S099.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S099.text: - P01-S099 INTERPRETATION (zero volume; from P01-S018, P01-S063): a series whose volumes are all 0 (or defaulted to 0 by `from_kite`) gives no volume nodes, so no zone gets the volume vote; nothing else in the four files reads volume. Where only some volumes are 0, the profile is computed from the others without any sign that values were missing (A05 AUDIT HA-08).
P01-S099.sec: 7. Input-order, data-quality and numeric edge cases across the four files (summary)

P01-S100.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S100.text: - P01-S100 INTERPRETATION (short series and single candles; from P01-S039, P01-S060 to P01-S063): with `left = right = 5` a series needs at least 11 bars before any pivot can be found; a shorter series yields no pivots and no zones for that timeframe. A single candle with `high > low` and a positive volume gives exactly one volume node (the centre of the bucket that holds the middle of its own range); with a zero volume it gives none (`peak <= 0`); a single zero-range candle gives none (`hi <= lo`).
P01-S100.sec: 7. Input-order, data-quality and numeric edge cases across the four files (summary)

P01-S101.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P01-S101.text: - P01-S101 FACT and INTERPRETATION (units, across the four files): every tolerance is a percentage of a price and none uses ATR, a tick size or an absolute amount (apart from the round-number test's floating-point allowances of `1e-9`, P01-S085 (a)): `cluster_pct` is relative to the previous pivot's price (P01-S053), `merge_pct` to the group's mean centre (P01-S072), `band_buffer_pct` and `buffer_pct` to the band's centre (P01-S024, P01-S083). The pivot window counts bars (P01-S040); the recency window counts calendar days (P01-S089); the volume bins are equal fractions of the window's price range (P01-S062). No value is rounded to a tick in the four files; only `to_dict` rounds, to four decimals (P01-S028).
P01-S101.sec: 7. Input-order, data-quality and numeric edge cases across the four files (summary)

P01-S125.label: INTERPRETATION

P01-S140.label: INTERPRETATION
P01-S140.text: - P01-S140 INTERPRETATION (the round-number vote on the test inputs; added by the P01 checker; code reading of P01-S084 and P01-S085 applied to the test values, with `math.log10(100.0) = 2.0`, P01-S133; no test was run): the bands of the tests at L98 to L101 (100.0 to 100.0), L104 to L108 (100.0 to 100.2) and L111 to L115 (100.0 to 100.5) have centres from 100 to 100.25, so the magnitude is 100 and the band contains 100.0, a multiple of the step; `_has_round_number` is then `True` and each of these groups also gets `("round_number", 0.5)`. Each test's assertion holds either way. The HIGH test's merged band, 519.8 to 520.2, contains no multiple of 50, so no round-number vote applies there (score 6).

P01-S132.label: HISTORICAL
P01-S132.text: - P01-S132 HISTORICAL (the first commit's message, `dea336ae71c353fd86331a37d0a788e02968aca9`): "for every PLACED candidate it fetches Daily/60m/30m structure, scores S/R zones by confluence, flags buying-into-resistance (+ support/short mirror), and logs an evidence row to sr_detector_results for OFFLINE validation. INTERPRETATION: at the time of writing, the stated use of the scores was offline validation; later code reuses the same zones and confidence labels for the V2 retest divert (`screening/retest_monitor.py` L384 to L387), the structure exit (`orders/structure_exit_manager.py` L266 to L277) and the V3 consumers (P01-S109 to P01-S111), behind their own flags (their owners' logic).

P01-AP01.text: - P01-AP01 — What makes a zone HIGH: SR-C3, the configuration comment L526 and the first commit's message require "≥2 distinct method-types", and the module docstring says confidence is "NEVER a single method — it is a weighted sum of independent votes"; in the code `swing_pivots` and `multi_tf` are always present, both derived from the swing pivots, so the method-type condition is always met with the committed weights, every group present on all three timeframes is HIGH, and a two-timeframe group with three touches is HIGH, with no volume, prior-day, round-number or recency vote (P01-S076 to P01-S080, P01-S121, P01-S124, P01-S125). The test that defines HIGH treats `multi_tf` as one of the two methods. Does the code meet the stated meaning of confidence? (Boundary: the consumers that act on HIGH, the flags, the retest divert and the structure exit, are other parts' and A11's.)

P01-AP02.text: - P01-AP02 — Plateaus and outside bars: SR-P1's parenthesis says a "perfectly flat plateau does not mark every bar", and the docstring says a bar yields both a HIGH and a LOW only "in degenerate single-bar windows"; in the code every bar of a plateau with lower bars around it becomes a pivot, and an outside bar yields both, so touches can count one swing several times (P01-S041 to P01-S043, P01-S056, P01-S122). Is the touch count what SR-Z2 ("touches = count of pivots") intends?

P01-AP03.text: - P01-AP03 — Width of a zone and of a merged group: clustering chains without a width limit (as SR-Z1 states), the merge compares with a drifting group mean, and the merge joins zones of one timeframe too, against SR-C1's "ACROSS timeframes"; the merged band is the union, gaps included (P01-S053, P01-S072, P01-S074, P01-S120). Is an unbounded band within the design?

P01-AP04.text: - P01-AP04 — Zero-width zones: a single pivot, or pivots at one price, make a zone with `band_low == band_high`, against the `Zone` docstring "A price BAND (never a single line)"; such zones are scored and emitted (LOW, or MEDIUM with a round number and full recency, or with a volume or prior-day vote), and the round-number test on them needs an exact multiple (P01-S054, P01-S079 (d), P01-S085 (d)).

P01-AP05.text: - P01-AP05 — Candle order (A05 CM-05's A08 side; boundary: A05 for the broker's rows, A18 for the regime and the V3 runners, A07 for `gate_htf`): no step sorts or checks the order; `find_swing_pivots` uses list position as time, which leaves the zones unchanged for a descending series but reverses the output order that the regime engine and the V3 runners' `gate_htf` read as time, and for any other order takes positional neighbours that are not time neighbours; the fetch test's fixture is descending; `prior_day_levels` assumes ascending order (P01-S021, P01-S045, P01-S094, P01-S108, P01-S126, P01-S135).

P01-AP06.text: - P01-AP06 — Duplicates and gaps: a duplicated bar can add a touch and doubles its volume in the profile; gaps are not detected (P01-S046, P01-S095). No source states how they were to be handled.

P01-AP07.text: - P01-AP07 — Unvalidated values (A05 CM-10 and HA-08, A08's side): `from_kite` validates nothing and defaults a missing or `None` volume to 0; NaN silently suppresses pivots, while NaN or an infinity can raise `ValueError` or `OverflowError` in `volume_profile_nodes` and `_has_round_number`; mixed naive and aware times raise in two `max` calls; none of the four files catches an exception, and one bad row discards a whole interval in the fetcher (P01-S017 to P01-S019, P01-S047, P01-S058, P01-S064, P01-S086, P01-S097). Which caller handles each exception is the callers' logic (section 8).

P01-AP08.text: - P01-AP08 — Recency time base: a `None` clock (a `_safe_now` that caught an exception, or a caller that passes none) or a non-positive window gives every dated zone the full recency vote rather than none; age is in calendar days; the time-zone branch strips both sides to wall-clock digits, which gives the elapsed time only when both wall clocks are IST, and the export script's naive 15:30 `as_of` takes that branch whenever the candle labels are aware; `recency_min_factor` above 1 escapes the upper clamp (P01-S088 to P01-S091, P01-S137). Is full credit on a missing clock intended?

P01-AP09.text: - P01-AP09 — The buffer: the `ScoringParams` default `band_buffer_pct` is 0.0 while the zone builder, the loader and the committed file give 0.1, so the unit tests score without the buffer the configured path uses; SR-C2 does not mention the buffer, and the round-number test uses none (P01-S069, P01-S083, P01-S084, P01-S120, P01-S124).

P01-AP10.text: - P01-AP10 — Zero-weight votes: the volume, prior-day and round-number votes are recorded and counted as method-types even with a weight of 0 (latent at the committed weights) (P01-S081).

P01-AP11.text: - P01-AP11 — The round-number rule: the step is half the power of ten below the band's centre, so the "magnitude" step adds nothing and the step jumps tenfold at each power of ten (from 5 per cent to 50 per cent of price), against the docstring "A multiple of the price magnitude (or half-magnitude)" (P01-S084, P01-S085). A second, related rule lives in `round_number_levels` (boundary: zone-builder part; P01-S087).

P01-AP12.text: - P01-AP12 — Output order and the logged zones (boundary: the detector part): `score_zones` returns zones by ascending centre, and the detector logs the first twelve of each kind in that order, so with more zones the lowest-priced are kept, not the strongest or nearest (P01-S070, P01-S093).

P01-AP13.text: - P01-AP13 — The volume profile's input (boundary: zone-builder part): nodes come from the daily bars, or from the first series when there is no daily one (the PB-01 watchlist capture fetches only 60-minute and 30-minute bars), each bar's whole volume at its mid; `bins` and `node_frac` are not validated (P01-S062 to P01-S066, P01-S111).

P01-AP14.text: - P01-AP14 — The confidence class (boundary: A18 for the V3 consumers, the retest and structure-exit parts and A11 for theirs): the comment L169 to L174 says swings are "NOT-YET-VALIDATED until Rama's manual-marking validation passes" and that "The 03.03 R:R gate will use ANCHOR-only levels for live capital until then"; no code sets the validated class, and nothing in the four files restricts the use of swing-derived zones, which the V3 runners use for their stop and target edges while labelling the record `ANCHOR_ONLY` (`v3_chain/runner.py` L186 to L196, with its gates commented "LOG-ONLY — recorded, never enforced", L207; the PB-01 runner's target edge, `v3_chain/pb01_runner.py` L136 to L138) and which the V2 retest divert and the structure exit would use when their flags are on (P01-S035, P01-S107, P01-S109, P01-S110, P01-S116, P01-S132).

P01-AP15.text: - P01-AP15 — Lag of recent structure: the last `right` bars can never be pivots (as SR-P2 states), which with the committed `n` of 5 means the newest possible touch is five bars old on each timeframe (P01-S040, P01-S048).

V3 03.01: the Layer-A intraday anchors (VWAP/ORB) need TODAY's fine bars (e.g. 5-minute, lookback 1) — a different window than the multi-day structural fetch. Reuses the same token/cache/fetch_fn machinery; returns None on any failure (fail-safe, SR-F4). fetch_timeframes() is unchanged."

P02-S018.label: FACT
P02-S018.text: - P02-S018 FACT (`fetch_by_token`, L85 to L101): `if not token: return None` (L98 to L99), with no log line; then `key = cache_key or f"__token_{int(token)}"` (L100) and `return self._fetch_one(key, int(token), interval, lookback_days=lookback_days)` (L101). The key takes the place of the symbol in the cache key and in the WARNING text of `_fetch_one`. Docstring L89 to L97: the index "is NOT in the instrument cache, so its token is supplied from config and fetched directly through the SAME rate-limited fetch_fn (reuse, not a new data path). Returns None on any failure (fail-safe). `cache_key` scopes the intra-session cache (defaults to the token)."

P02-S019.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S019.text: - P02-S019 INTERPRETATION (`fetch_by_token`'s edge cases; from L98 to L101 and P01-S005): `int(token)` at L100 (when no `cache_key` is given) and at L101 runs outside any `try`, so a truthy token that `int` cannot convert raises `ValueError` or `TypeError` (corrected in the check: or `OverflowError` for an infinite float, P01-S005) to the caller, against the docstring's "Returns None on any failure"; a fractional float token is truncated; a negative token is used as given. A `cache_key` equal to a symbol that `fetch_timeframes` or `fetch_interval` uses on the same fetcher object would share that symbol's entries. The one non-test caller, `regime/engine.py` L321 to L326 (A18's; interface), passes an `int` token (cast at L78) and no `cache_key`, inside its own `try` that logs a WARNING "regime: index fetch failed".

P02-S020.label: FACT
P02-S020.text: - P02-S020 FACT (`_resolve_token`, L105 to L112): inside a `try`: `row = self._cache.get_by_symbol(symbol)` (L107), `token = int(getattr(row, "instrument_token"))` (L108), `return token or None` (L109); any exception (comment L110: "InstrumentNotFoundError or anything") is logged as WARNING "sr_detector fetch: token lookup failed for %s: %s" with the symbol and the exception, and `None` is returned (L110 to L112). A token of 0 therefore gives `None` without any log line: the WARNING is written only when an exception occurs (A05 IN-02 records the same at its boundary).

P02-S021.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S021.text: - P02-S021 INTERPRETATION (the cases; from L105 to L112, P02-S005 (e)): a symbol missing from the instrument cache (the cache's exception, A05's), a row without the attribute (`AttributeError`) and a row whose token is `None` (`TypeError`) are logged and give no candles; a row with token 0 gives no candles silently; a negative token is passed on as a token; the symbol string is used exactly as given (no case or whitespace normalisation). The instrument cache is called with no lock of the fetcher; its own thread safety and its handling of placeholder rows are A05's (IN-02, IN-09).

P02-S022.label: FACT
P02-S022.text: - P02-S022 FACT (`_fetch_one`, L114 to L136, in order): `cached = self._cache_get(symbol, interval)` (L118) runs first and outside the `try`; a non-`None` result is returned at once (L119 to L120). Inside the `try` (L121 to L129): `now = self._now_fn()` (L122); `lb = self._lookback_days if lookback_days is None else int(lookback_days)` (L123); `from_dt = now - timedelta(days=lb)` (L124); `rows = self._fetch_fn(token, from_dt, now, interval)` (L125); `candles = [Candle.from_kite(r) for r in (rows or [])]` (L126); `if candles: self._cache_put(symbol, interval, candles)` (L127 to L128); `return candles or None` (L129). `except Exception as exc` logs the WARNING of P02-S037 and returns `None` (L130 to L136).

P02-S023.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S023.text: - P02-S023 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the window; from L122 to L125): FACT: the window is from `now − lb` days to `now`, where `now` is the injected clock read at the moment of the miss and `lb` the call's lookback or, if none, the constructor's; `timedelta(days=lb)` counts calendar days. FACT: no market hours, session open or close, trading calendar, weekend, holiday or "today" is applied, and neither end is rounded to a bar or day boundary. INTERPRETATION: `to` is the current moment, so the window includes the current session up to the call; `from` falls at the same wall-clock time `lb` calendar days earlier, so a 180-day window covers about 180 calendar days of whatever sessions the broker returns; an explicit `lookback_days=0` gives `from == to`, and a negative value puts `from` after `to`; neither is rejected. FACT (time zone): every non-test construction in the trading process passes `time_authority.now_ist` (section 3.8), which returns `datetime.now(tz=_IST)` with `_IST_OFFSET = timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30)` and `_IST = timezone(_IST_OFFSET, name="IST")` (`core/time_authority.py` L58 to L59, L94 to L99; interface; quotation corrected in the check), so the closure receives two aware IST datetimes; the export script's per-call detector passes a constant naive time instead (P01-S137; P05's). How the library turns the datetimes into the request's `from` and `to` is A05's; the vendor page states no time zone for them (P02-S004).

P02-S024.label: INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED
P02-S024.text: - P02-S024 INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (a still-forming last candle; from L122 to L129): the fetcher applies no as-of truncation and no completeness test: whatever the answer to a window ending "now" contains is converted, cached and returned as received, including, if the broker sent one, a still-forming last intraday candle or today's daily candle during the session. Whether the legacy server's answers contained such a candle is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 HA-04; P01-S096); the vendor page's example says only that the latest record reflects the time of the request (P02-S004). The consequences for the zones are P01-S096's; for the prior-day levels and the anchors, P02-S048 and P02-S058.

P02-S025.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S025.text: - P02-S025 FACT and INTERPRETATION (conversion; P01-S015 to P01-S019): the rows are converted with `Candle.from_kite` in the order the closure returned them (L126); the comprehension is inside the `try`, so one row that `from_kite` cannot convert (a missing key, a `None` or non-numeric price, a non-integral volume string) makes the whole interval `None` with one WARNING, and no row is skipped individually (P01-S019); NaN and infinite prices pass through (P01-S017). `rows or []` turns `None`, an empty list or any other falsy answer into an empty list. INTERPRETATION: a truthy answer that is not a list of dictionaries (for example a dictionary, which iterates over its keys) fails in `from_kite` and is logged as "historical_data failed".
P02-S025.sec: 3.5 Row conversion, ordering and empty results

P02-S026.label: FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED
P02-S026.text: - P02-S026 FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (ordering, duplicates, gaps, validation: A05 CM-05's A08 side): FACT: no line of the four files sorts candles, removes duplicates, detects gaps, checks that timestamps increase, compares a candle's date with the request, or checks the values; `fetch.py` converts and caches the list in the closure's order (L126 to L128) and returns the same list on a cache hit (L147); `zone_builder.py` passes each series to the calculation core unchanged (L94 to L97, L99 to L103), takes `daily[-2]` as the prior day by position (L81) and filters the anchors' bars by date and time (L160 to L163, L172). INTERPRETATION: the zones and the volume profile do not depend on order except through the pivots (P01-S045, P01-S094); `prior_day_levels` assumes an ascending series (P02-S048); the anchors' filters and `max`/`min` do not depend on order; a duplicated candle is counted twice by the pivots, the volume profile and the VWAP (P01-S095; `session_vwap` sums every bar given that has a positive volume, `core/candle_math.py` L149 to L155, A05's; corrected in the check). Whether the legacy server's rows were always ascending and unique is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 CM-05; P01-U02). The fetch test's fixture rows are newest first (P01-S126).
P02-S026.sec: 3.5 Row conversion, ordering and empty results

P02-S027.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S027.text: - P02-S027 FACT and INTERPRETATION (empty results; from L126 to L129 and `main.py` L429 to L430): FACT: an empty or `None` answer gives an empty list, which is not cached (L127) and is returned as `None` (L129), with no log line, because the WARNING is written only in the `except` branch; the closure returns `[]` when the market-data handle is `None`, so a missing handle gives the same silent `None` (A05 HA-09 records the related call-site text). INTERPRETATION: within the fetcher an empty answer, a missing handle and an answer whose every row was dropped (impossible here: no row is dropped) are indistinguishable and leave no trace; there is no negative cache, so every later call for the same key asks the closure again.
P02-S027.sec: 3.5 Row conversion, ordering and empty results

P02-S028.label: FACT
P02-S028.text: - P02-S028 FACT (key and value; L138 to L151): `_cache_put` stores `self._mem[(symbol, interval)] = (self._now_fn(), candles)` while holding the lock (L149 to L151). `_cache_get` reads `entry = self._mem.get((symbol, interval))` while holding the lock (L139 to L140), returns `None` when there is no entry (L141 to L142), then, outside the lock, computes `age = (self._now_fn() - fetched_at).total_seconds()` (L143 to L144), returns `None` when `age > self._cache_ttl_sec` (L145 to L146) and otherwise the stored list (L147). The key is the pair (first argument of `_fetch_one`, interval): the symbol for `fetch_timeframes` and `fetch_interval`, the `cache_key` or `__token_<n>` for `fetch_by_token` (L100 to L101). The key does not contain the lookback, the window's start or end, the token or the clock reading; the value is the candle list and the clock reading at the time of storing.
P02-S028.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S029.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S029.text: - P02-S029 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the clock of the age): FACT: the age is the difference of two readings of the injected `now_fn`, the stored one taken at `_cache_put` (L151) and the current one at `_cache_get` (L144); in the trading process every construction passes `time_authority.now_ist` (section 3.8), that is `datetime.now(tz=_IST)` (P02-S023). No monotonic clock is used anywhere in the four files (P02-S009). The comment L49 calls the stored value "fetched_at_monotonic_dt" (A05 HA-06 records the same difference). INTERPRETATION (current external context, P02-S005 (c) and (d); basis corrected in the check): `datetime.now(tz)` is documented as returning "the current local date and time", "converted to *tz*'s time zone"; `today()`, of which `now()` is the form with a `tz` parameter, is "Equivalent to: `datetime.fromtimestamp(time.time())`"; and `time.time()` "can return a lower value than a previous call if the system clock has been set back between the two calls"; the age therefore follows the system's wall clock, unlike `time.monotonic()`, which is "not affected by system clock updates". The page does not state the clock source of `now(tz)` in other words; this reading rests on those sentences.
P02-S029.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S030.label: INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED
P02-S030.text: - P02-S030 INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (what a wall-clock age means; from P02-S028, P02-S029 and P02-S005 (c)): a backward step of the system clock makes the computed age smaller, or negative, so an entry is served for longer than the TTL; a forward step expires entries early. The age is calendar time, not market time: an entry ages at the same rate across the close, the night, weekends and holidays, and nothing ties an entry to a session (an entry stored at 15:20 is still served at 15:45 within 1800 s, whatever happened in the market meanwhile). A daily list stored early in a session keeps whatever last candle it held (P02-S024) for up to the TTL. Whether the legacy machine's clock stepped while the system ran is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 HA-06; A17).
P02-S030.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S031.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S031.text: - P02-S031 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the TTL test and a TTL of 0; from L145): FACT: the test is `age > ttl`, so an entry whose age equals the TTL is still served. FACT: the watchlist fetcher and the one-minute fetcher are built with `cache_ttl_sec=0.0` (`main.py` L3732, L3777; section 3.8). INTERPRETATION: with a TTL of 0 an entry is served only when the computed age is 0 or negative, that is, when the read falls within the clock's resolution of the store or after a backward clock step; otherwise every call goes to the closure. Each successful fetch is still stored (L127 to L128) and kept (P02-S032). A negative TTL serves an entry only when the computed age is at or below that negative value, that is, after a backward clock step of at least the TTL's magnitude (corrected in the check; the writer had "never serves"). The datetime page notes that "Subsequent calls to `datetime.now()` may return the same instant depending on the precision of the underlying clock" (P02-S005 (d)).
P02-S031.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S032.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S032.text: - P02-S032 FACT and INTERPRETATION (no eviction, no bound; from L49 to L51, L138 to L151): FACT: no line removes an entry from `_mem`: `_cache_get` skips a stale entry but leaves it in place, and the only write is the overwrite by `_cache_put` after the next successful fetch of the same key; there is no size limit, no eviction, no clear method and no end-of-day reset. INTERPRETATION: each fetcher object keeps one candle list per distinct (key, interval) for its whole life, which for the fetchers built in `main.py` is the life of the process; the memory held grows with the number of distinct symbols fetched, and a stale list whose refetch keeps failing stays in memory, unused, until the process ends.
P02-S032.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S033.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S033.text: - P02-S033 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the same list object is shared; from L147, L151): FACT: a cache hit returns the stored list object itself, not a copy; the `Candle` objects are frozen (P01-S014), the list is not. INTERPRETATION: every caller of one fetcher object within the TTL receives the same list, so a caller that sorted, appended to or removed from it would change what later callers receive; no function in the four files changes a list it receives (`zone_builder.py` reads its series and builds new lists, `scoped` and `window`, L160 to L163, L172; no function of the calculation core modifies its arguments, P01-S010, P01-S044); the callers in other parts and topics handle the list by their own logic (the retest monitor builds a new list, `screening/retest_monitor.py` L220 to L225, P04's; the V3 and PB-01 consumers' truncation is A18's).
P02-S033.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S034.label: FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED
P02-S034.text: - P02-S034 FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (thread safety; from L51, L118 to L151): FACT: the one `threading.Lock` is held only for the dictionary read (L139 to L140) and the dictionary write (L150 to L151); the instrument-cache lookup, the clock reads at L122 and L144, the closure call, the conversion and the logging run without it. INTERPRETATION (P02-S005 (b)): the dictionary is safe for concurrent use by several threads; the class does not serialize fetches: two threads that miss on the same key at about the same time both call the closure and both store, the later store replacing the earlier (no single-flight and no in-flight marker), and calls on one fetcher object, or on different fetcher objects built over the one closure, can be in the closure at the same time. Which threads use which object is in section 3.8; whether calls overlapped in production, and whether the shared client tolerated it, is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A01 C38a; A04 RL-11).
P02-S034.sec: 3.6 The cache: key, value, clock, TTL, eviction, sharing, locking

P02-S035.label: FACT
P02-S035.text: - P02-S035 FACT (what the fail-safe covers; from L114 to L136, L105 to L112, L98 to L101): one `except Exception` (L130) covers L122 to L129: the clock read, the lookback conversion, the window arithmetic, the closure (the limiter and the broker call), the conversion of every row and `_cache_put` with its clock read. `_resolve_token` has its own `except Exception` (L110). Outside both: `_cache_get` at L118 (its dictionary lookup at L140, whose key is the symbol or cache key and the interval, its clock read at L144 and the subtraction), the loop over `intervals` in `fetch_timeframes` (L64; the dictionary lookup and the loop added in the check) and, in `fetch_by_token`, the two `int(token)` calls (L100 to L101). Exceptions that derive from `BaseException` but not from `Exception` (`KeyboardInterrupt`, `SystemExit`, `GeneratorExit`; P02-S005 (f)) are not caught anywhere in the file.
P02-S035.sec: 3.7 Failures, logging, retries and the rate limiter

P02-S036.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S036.text: - P02-S036 INTERPRETATION (the paths that can raise to the caller, against "never raise"; from P02-S035): an exception raised by `now_fn` at L144, or a `TypeError` from subtracting a naive stored reading from an aware current one (P02-S005 (d)), propagates out of `fetch_timeframes`, `fetch_interval` and `fetch_by_token`, against SR-F4's "nothing propagates into the pipeline", the module docstring's "never raise" and the methods' docstrings ("never raises"; "returns None on any failure"); it can happen only when an entry exists for the key (L141 to L142); with one `now_fn` per object the two readings have the same form, so this path needs the clock function itself to raise: `time_authority.now_ist` is a plain `datetime.now(tz=_IST)` with no handler (`core/time_authority.py` L94 to L99), which would raise only if the underlying clock read failed; another clock function could raise more readily. The `int(token)` escape is P02-S019's. Conversely, a failure inside `_cache_put` after a successful broker call (L128) is caught and reported with the text "historical_data failed", and the fetched candles are discarded. Added in the check: argument types that no non-test caller passes (an unhashable symbol, cache key or interval at L140, or an `intervals` value that cannot be iterated at L64) would also raise outside the `try`; every non-test caller passes strings and lists of strings (P02-S040).
P02-S036.sec: 3.7 Failures, logging, retries and the rate limiter

P02-S037.label: FACT
P02-S037.text: - P02-S037 FACT (the log lines; from L111, L131 to L135, L153 to L159): the file writes two log lines only: WARNING "sr_detector fetch: token lookup failed for %s: %s" (symbol, exception; L111) and WARNING "sr_detector fetch: historical_data failed for %s/%s: %s" (symbol or cache key, interval, exception; L131 to L135), the second for every exception in `_fetch_one`, whatever its type. Nothing is logged at INFO or DEBUG; a cache hit, a miss, an empty answer, a token of 0 and a missing handle log nothing; no counter, alert, event or telemetry is written. `_safe_log` (L153 to L159) does nothing when the logger is `None` and swallows any exception raised by the logger call.
P02-S037.sec: 3.7 Failures, logging, retries and the rate limiter

P02-S038.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S038.text: - P02-S038 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the limiter's outcomes and broker errors through the fetcher; A04 RL-05, A05 HA-01; interface for A04's files): FACT: the closure's `rate_limiter.acquire("historical")` (`main.py` L431) "Block[s] until n tokens are available" and raises `ValueError` for an unknown category, `BrokerRateLimitError` when the request exceeds the bucket's capacity or "max_wait_sec elapsed without acquiring n tokens", and `RateLimitAbortedError` when the shutdown event is set during the wait (`broker/rate_limiter.py` L177 to L185, L191, L215, L239; the `ValueError` itself is raised at L170, in `_get_bucket`, added in the check); `BrokerRateLimitError` derives from `BrokerError` and `RateLimitAbortedError` from `TradingSystemError`, both from `Exception` (`core/exceptions.py` L30, L158, L243, L284); the docstring of `RateLimitAbortedError` reads "INFO (not WARN/ERROR): shutdown is an expected operation, not a failure" (L284 to L292). FACT: each of these reaches L130 and is logged with the one WARNING text of P02-S037, "historical_data failed", although `historical_data` was not called, and the interval gives `None`. An exception raised by the library inside `historical_data` (a broker refusal such as an HTTP 429, a timeout, an authentication fault) reaches the same handler with the same text and level; the fetcher calls no `penalize`, freezes nothing and counts nothing (a search of the sixteen A08 paths for `penal`, `429` and `throttl` finds no line). INTERPRETATION: the cause of a failure can be read only from the exception text at the end of the WARNING.
P02-S038.sec: 3.7 Failures, logging, retries and the rate limiter

P02-S039.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S039.text: - P02-S039 FACT and INTERPRETATION (retries, pacing and whose thread waits): FACT: the four files contain no retry, backoff, sleep or wait on the fetch path; the only pacing is the closure's `acquire` (A04's); a failed interval is asked again only by the next call that misses on it (no negative cache, P02-S027). INTERPRETATION: the whole time of a fetch (a limiter wait of up to the limiter's `max_wait_sec`, then the broker call up to the client's timeout, then the conversion) is spent on the thread that called the public method: the V1 detector's worker, the warmer's worker, the retest monitor's thread, the A18 consumers' threads and the export script's main thread (section 3.8); `fetch_timeframes` makes up to one such call per interval, one after another. The dispatcher thread never calls the fetcher (section 6).
P02-S039.sec: 3.7 Failures, logging, retries and the rate limiter

INTERPRETATION: the second-to-last element is taken as the prior day, which assumes an ascending series whose last element is the current day: (a) if the series ends with a candle for today (forming during the session, if the broker returns one, P02-S024), `daily[-2]` is the previous trading day; (b) if it ends with the previous trading day (no candle for today: a call before the open or on a holiday, or an answer without today's candle), `daily[-2]` is the trading day before that, two sessions back; (c) a one-candle series gives that candle itself; (d) a descending series gives the second-oldest candle; (e) a duplicated last candle gives its duplicate. Which case applied in production is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 HA-04; P02-S024). P02-S054.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S054.text: - P02-S054 INTERPRETATION (the rule and its edges; from L130 to L140, P01-S005, P01-S133): (a) the result holds the multiples of the power of ten and of its half at or below the price and the next multiple above each, which are three values: in exact arithmetic, with M the power of ten at or below the price and b the multiple of M at or below it, the first step gives {b, b + M} and the second {b, b + M/2} or {b + M/2, b + M}, so the union is always b, b + M/2 and b + M; the rounding to six decimals can merge two of them only for a price below 0.00001, and floating-point division can shift the set by one half step for a price that is exactly a multiple (a plain-expression check on 26-Nov-2026: `0.3 / 0.1` gives 2.9999999999999996, so 0.3 would give (0.2, 0.25, 0.3)) (corrected in the check: the writer had "two to four values"); for 523 the code gives (500, 550, 600), as the docstring says; (b) a price exactly on a multiple lists itself as the lower level (500 gives (500, 550, 600)), so the level just below it (450) is not listed; (c) the step depends on the decade of the price and jumps tenfold at each power of ten, as for the confluence test `_has_round_number`, which uses the same two steps on a band (P01-S085, P01-S087); (d) a NaN price passes the guard (`nan <= 0` is false) and `math.floor(math.log10(nan))` raises `ValueError`, and a `+inf` price raises `OverflowError`; neither is caught in the function, in `build_anchor_payload` (L199) or at the detector's call (`sr_detector/detector.py` L235, outside its `try` of L220 to L234; P03's logic), against the docstring's "returns () for a missing/non-positive price". The detector's reference price is `float(candidate.intended_entry)` when that value is truthy (L215), and NaN and infinity are truthy (P01-S133); A06 WA-07 records that a NaN or infinite trigger price can be queued with a signal; whether such a value reaches `intended_entry` is the price path's (A06; P04).

Docstring L151 to L159: "Scopes `fine_candles` to `on_date`'s in-session bars, then: - vwap = core.candle_math.session_vwap over the scoped bars; - orb_high / orb_low = max high / min low over the OPENING window [session_open, session_open + orb_window_minutes).
