P02-S057.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S057.text: - P02-S057 INTERPRETATION (what a label is taken to mark: P02's secondary side of A05-17 and A05 HA-03; from L162 and L172): the scope keeps a bar labelled `session_open` and drops one labelled `session_close`, and the opening window keeps the bars labelled before `session_open + orb_window_minutes`. Read with the broker's label as the start of the bar (A05's reading, P01-S058), a 15-minute window from 09:15 keeps the 5-minute bars labelled 09:15, 09:20 and 09:25, which cover 09:15 to 09:30, and the session's last bar is the one labelled 15:25. Read with the label as the end of the bar, the same rule would keep a bar labelled 09:15 that covers 09:10 to 09:15, before the open, and drop the bar that ends at the close. The code's rule therefore fits the start reading; the test `tests/unit/test_sr_anchors.py` L52 to L62 states it ("ORB window 15 min = first 3 candles (09:15/09:20/09:25)"). No A08 line states the meaning of `ts` beyond the `Candle` docstring (P01-S014); A05-17's history question stays OPEN as recorded (P07-S075).

With the committed values (zone TTL 1800 s, re-warm margin 300 s, fetcher TTL 1800 s; values only): a symbol warmed with a fresh fetch at time t becomes due at an age of 1500 s; that re-warm, at about t + 1500 s, finds the fetcher's lists about 1500 s old, still inside its TTL, rebuilds the zones from the same candles (only the recency vote moves with `now`, P01-S089) and resets `warmed_at`; the next re-warm, at about t + 3000 s, misses the fetcher's cache and fetches anew. In this cycle a `ZoneSet` that `get` reports as at most about 1500 s old can rest on candles about 3000 s old; at the extreme (a re-warm delayed until expiry) the candles can be up to the sum of the two TTLs, 3600 s, plus the time of the fetch and the scoring, older than the read. A warm triggered by a signal's arrival inside the fetcher's TTL has the same effect. Nothing in the `ZoneSet` records the candles' age, so a reader cannot see it.

P02-S083.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S083.text: - P02-S083 INTERPRETATION (the loop; from L103 to L119 and P02-S005): one worker thread takes the symbols one at a time in arrival order; the re-warm scan runs only after the queue has been empty for `idle_sleep_sec` (2.0 s), so a steady stream of new symbols postpones it; an `Exception` raised in `warm` (for example by the fetcher's clock path, P02-S036, by the scoring on NaN or infinite candle values, P01-S097, or by the cache's `put`, P02-S065) is logged and the loop goes on; an exception that derives from `BaseException` only would end the thread without a line of the warmer's own (P02-S005 (f)); the stop flag is read only between items and after each idle wait, so a stop takes effect after the current warm. `task_done` is called for every item taken, the sentinel included; nothing in the package calls the queue's `join` (search), so the counter has no reader.

P02-S084.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S084.text: - P02-S084 FACT and INTERPRETATION (`_enqueue_rewarms`, L121 to L126, and the re-warm rule): FACT: inside a `try`, `for sym in self._cache.symbols_due_for_rewarm(self._rewarm_margin_sec): self.enqueue(sym)` (L122 to L124); any exception is logged as ERROR "zone_warmer: rewarm scan failed: %s" (L125 to L126). INTERPRETATION (from P02-S067, P02-S068 and P02-S073): a symbol is due when its `ZoneSet` is at least `ttl − margin` old (with the committed 1800 and 300, 1500 s; values only), expired entries included, and every stored symbol stays stored; so every symbol warmed once is re-warmed about every `ttl − margin` seconds (plus the idle wait and the warm's own time) for the life of the process, after the close, at night and on holidays included: no line of the warmer or the cache tests market hours, the session or the date. In the committed-value cycle of P02-S070 alternate re-warms are served from the fetcher's cache and the others fetch afresh, three broker calls each through the shared `historical` bucket. A symbol whose re-warm gets no interval at all (every interval failed or was empty, or the token lookup failed: a fetch miss, which leaves the entry alone, P02-S086) keeps its old `warmed_at`, so it stays due and is queued again at every idle scan, about every 2 s plus the time of the failed fetch, until a fetch returns at least one interval (a partial result is stored and resets `warmed_at`, P02-S086); each attempt asks the closure again for every interval (no negative cache, P02-S027) and so takes a `historical` token for each, except when the token lookup failed or the market-data handle is `None`, where the limiter is not reached (P02-S013, P02-S020); it logs a WARNING in the fetcher for each failed interval (none for an empty answer; one "token lookup failed" for a failed lookup) and an INFO "fetch miss" in the warmer (precision added in the check: the writer had "a symbol whose re-warm fetch fails" and "each attempt goes through the limiter"). A stored symbol whose warm raises (P02-S083) also keeps its old entry and stays due, and if the cause repeats (for example the same cached candles failing in the scoring), the ERROR "warm error" recurs at every idle scan. A margin larger than the TTL would make every stored symbol due at every scan, and a negative margin would re-warm only after expiry. The module docstring says "Re-warms cached symbols before TTL expiry" (L10).

P02-S089.label: INTERPRETATION
P02-S089.text: - P02-S089 INTERPRETATION (shutdown; from L71 to L80, L103 to L119 and P02-S005 (b)): the sentinel wakes a worker that waits in `get`; a worker inside a broker call (P02-S039) is not interrupted, so `join` returns after 2.0 s without it when the call lasts longer; that daemon thread then completes its warm, which can still write to the cache and log after `stop` has returned, and leaves its loop, or it is "abruptly stopped" when the interpreter exits (P02-S005 (b)). A limiter wait ends early only through the limiter's own shutdown event (`RateLimitAbortedError`, P02-S038), which the fetcher logs as a WARNING "historical_data failed". Corrected in the check (the writer counted a limiter wait among the waits that `stop` does not interrupt; interface for A01's file): in the trading process that event is the module's `_shutdown_event` (`main.py` L116, passed to the limiter at L2348), which `_shutdown` sets first ("FIX-060: Set shutdown event FIRST so rate limiter aborts immediately", L1628 to L1629), before it stops the warmer at L1744; so by then a limiter wait on the warmer's thread has already ended, and each later `acquire` that would have to wait aborts at once, with one WARNING per interval tried, while the worker goes on taking items until its own stop flag is set. `stop` neither drains nor clears the queue or `_pending`, so symbols still queued are not warmed. After `stop`, `enabled` is still true, so `enqueue` still accepts symbols into a queue that no worker reads; a `start` after a timed-out `stop` would start a second worker beside the first, because `_worker` was set to `None` (L80). P02-S101.label: FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED
P02-S101.text: - P02-S101 FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A01 C38a; P07-S020; A01 AUDIT L1867 to L1875; Audit Findings Register row "C38a (concurrency)": "MATCH; UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (component)", treatment "None decided (information only; no decision needed)", status "UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED", unchanged). Asked: how A08's fetchers call the one shared closure: which threads, how many fetcher objects, whether calls can overlap. A08 side: `OhlcFetcher` has seven constructions (six call sites; the one in `build_sr_detector` is reached from `main.py` and from the export script), six of them in the trading process over its one closure and the seventh in the export script's own process over that script's own closure; three are built at the committed values (P02-S040, P02-S041; corrected in the check: the writer had "seven construction sites build `OhlcFetcher` objects over the one closure"); the threads are those of P02-S091; each object calls the closure at L125 without holding its lock, with no serialization and no single-flight, so calls on one object, and on different objects, can be in the closure at the same time (P02-S034). In the trading process the A08 consumers' objects are each used by one thread (the V1 detector's "sr-detector", the warmer's "sr-zone-warmer", the retest monitor's "sr-retest-monitor"); the PB-01 object is shared by two A18 threads. Whether calls overlapped, and whether the client tolerated it, stays UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A04 RL-11, P02-S122).

P02-S102.label: FACT
P02-S102.text: - P02-S102 FACT (A02 K-23; P07-S026; A02 AUDIT L2128 to L2138; "ISSUE; FACT", "Batch T5 group G2 (AGREED, 09-Nov-2026)", "AGREED", unchanged). Asked: what bounds the warmer's queue, what happens when it is full, and whether any key reaches it. A08 side: the bound is the constructor default `max_queue: int = 512` (`sr_detector/zone_warmer.py` L42, L55), because `main.py` L3564 to L3568 passes no `max_queue` (P02-S075); no configuration key reaches it: `sr_detector.max_queue` (loader 256, not in the committed file) feeds only the V1 detector's queue (`sr_detector/detector.py` L100; P02-S076); a full queue drops the symbol with WARNING "zone_warmer: queue full, dropping %s" and removes it from `_pending`, so a later `enqueue` of the same symbol is tried again (L94 to L97; P02-S079). The idle sleep (2.0 s) and the enable flag are likewise constructor defaults that no key reaches (P02-S076). See P02-AP10.

P02-S103.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S103.text: - P02-S103 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A02 K-24; P07-S027; A02 AUDIT L2142 to L2152; "ISSUE; FACT; INTERPRETATION", "Batch T5 group G3 (AGREED, 09-Nov-2026)", "AGREED", unchanged). Asked: how each fetcher's lookback and cache time are set per construction, and which calls use the constructor's lookback. A08 side: P02-S040 gives each construction's lookback, TTL and clock. `fetch_timeframes` has no lookback parameter and always uses the constructor's (L53, L65, L123; P02-S015), so every structural and capture call uses it (rows 1, 3 to 6; for the PB-01 capture's daily fetch, the V3 section's `fetch_lookback_days`, 180, not `capture_fetch_lookback_days`, A02 K-24's point); only `fetch_interval` and `fetch_by_token` pass a lookback of their own (the anchors' 1 day; the PB-01 entry stage's 10, 60 and 1 days; the regime's 400 and 1 days). The regime fetcher's TTL is `sr_detector.cache_ttl_sec` (row 2); the V3 chain's is its own key (row 4); the PB-01 and one-minute fetchers have 0.0 in the code (rows 5 and 6). INTERPRETATION (boundary, A18's consumer): the regime runner's cadence, `compute_interval_sec` (committed 60.0, YAML L562), and its fetcher's TTL (`sr_detector.cache_ttl_sec`, committed 1800) come from different sections, so its intraday index list would be fetched at most once per TTL while the regime is computed every cadence (the class serves an entry until it is older than the TTL, P02-S028). See P02-AP14.

P02-S104.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P02-S104.text: - P02-S104 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A04 RL-05; P07-S041; A04 AUDIT L3435 to L3445; "ISSUE; FACT; INTERPRETATION", "A04 treatment group TG19 (AGREED, 13-Nov-2026)", "AGREED", unchanged). Asked: what the fetcher does with each exception the closure raises (limiter outcomes, broker errors, a 429), what it logs and returns, and what its callers then do. A08 side: every exception from the closure, the limiter's `ValueError`, `BrokerRateLimitError` and `RateLimitAbortedError` and any library error from `historical_data` (a 429 among them), is caught at L130, logged as the one WARNING "sr_detector fetch: historical_data failed for %s/%s: %s", and gives `None` for that interval; the fetcher has no 429 path, calls no `penalize` and counts nothing (P02-S037, P02-S038). The callers then see an omitted interval or `None`: the V1 detector makes its `FETCH_FAILED` analysis when every interval is missing (`sr_detector/detector.py` L169 to L174; P03), the warmer logs INFO "fetch miss" and leaves the cache as it was (P02-S085, P02-S086), the retest monitor gets no one-minute candles (P04), and the A18 consumers use their own fallbacks (`or {}`; the regime's UNKNOWN state, `regime/engine.py` L108 to L115). The record's MATCH part ("The fail-safe swallow itself matches SR-F4 (MATCH part, A08's)") agrees with these facts: no limiter or broker exception propagates; the two paths that can raise (P02-S019, P02-S036) involve neither the limiter nor the broker.

A08 side: `_resolve_token` turns a token of 0 into `None` with `return token or None` (L109) and writes no log line (the WARNING at L111 is only for an exception); `fetch_by_token` likewise returns `None` for a falsy token without a log (L98 to L99) (P02-S018, P02-S020). A token-0 symbol and a missing symbol therefore end the same way, the first silently and the second with a WARNING (P02-S021).

P02-AP01.text: - P02-AP01 — The fetcher cache's key does not contain the window (A05 HA-06's A08 side; evidence that bears on A05's KNOWN DEFECT consideration, which stands as recorded): the key is `(symbol or cache key, interval)` (P02-S028); since `536172cfadfdd28ec9e5f8c00f9d549f0cd57dc2` a call can choose its own window under that key (P02-S157); SR-F3 states the key and was written when each fetcher asked a window of one length per interval (P02-S142, P02-S155); `fetch_interval`'s docstring itself says its window is "a different window than the multi-day structural fetch" and that it "Reuses the same token/cache/fetch_fn machinery" (P02-S017, P02-S143). Where a second window for one key can arise inside a non-zero TTL: no committed construction; the V1 fetcher with the anchors on and `anchor_intraday_interval: 30minute`, a value the loader accepts and the YAML comment lists, where a failed structural `30minute` fetch followed by a successful one-day anchor fetch would give later structural requests one day of bars as their 180-day series, with no log line (P02-S042 (a)); the export script's per-call fetcher, whose clock is constant and whose `--interval` declares no `choices` and reaches the configuration copy through `model_copy`, which the current pydantic documentation says does not validate updated values (P02-S042 (c), P02-S160); the PB-01 fetcher only at a zero or negative age, with the TTL of 0 that the `main.py` comment gives as the means to keep the entry stage's 5-minute poll fresh (P02-S042 (b), P02-S148). For the AUDIT to weigh, on both sides (corrected in the check, which added A05's own reasoning beside the further facts): A05 HA-06 found its condition (d) to fail because SR-F3 states the very key and the `fetch_interval` docstring says it "Reuses the same token/cache/fetch_fn machinery", and its condition (c) to hold only under a documented but not committed setting (A05 AUDIT L1598); the further facts recorded here are that the key's fit to its requests changed with `536172cfadfdd28ec9e5f8c00f9d549f0cd57dc2`, that the same docstring states that the windows differ, and that the loader accepts `30minute` for both settings. No classification is given here. Sources: P02-S028, P02-S040 to P02-S042, P02-S108, P02-S142, P02-S143, P02-S148, P02-S155, P02-S157, P02-S160.

P02-AP02.text: - P02-AP02 — Wall-clock ages against the comment "monotonic" (fetcher and zone cache): the comment L49 names a monotonic time, while both caches age their entries by the injected wall clock (`now_ist`); a backward clock step serves entries beyond their TTL (and a TTL-0 entry at all), a forward step expires them early, and ages run through nights and holidays (P02-S029 to P02-S031, P02-S069, P02-S144). A05 HA-06 records the fetcher's side; the zone cache's side is not in an earlier record. Boundary: the machine's clock synchronisation is A17's.

P02-AP05.text: - P02-AP05 — Nothing is ever evicted: the fetcher's `_mem` and the zone cache's `_store` are never pruned or cleared; `evict_expired`, `size` and `clear` exist with no caller; nothing clears them at the end of the day or at shutdown (P02-S032, P02-S064, P02-S068, P02-S073). The memory held grows with the distinct symbols for the life of the process. The texts speak of "intra-session" re-fetch suppression and a cache "within the session" (P02-S143, P02-S149); no source states an entry's intended lifetime. Boundary: whether the process restarted daily, which would reset both, is A16's and A17's (P02-U10).

P02-AP06.text: - P02-AP06 — The re-warm rule re-warms every stored symbol without end: the scan returns expired entries too (`>=` a cutoff with no upper bound), so each symbol warmed once is re-warmed about every `ttl − margin` seconds for the life of the process, after the close and on holidays included, and a symbol whose re-warm gets no interval at all is queued again at every idle scan, about every 2 s plus the time of the failed fetch, each attempt asking the closure, and so the shared `historical` bucket, for every interval, except after a failed token lookup or without a market-data handle (P02-S067, P02-S084; precision added in the check). The docstrings say "Re-warms cached symbols before TTL expiry", "whose age exceeds (ttl − margin)" and "re-warm a cached symbol this long before its TTL expiry" (P02-S145, P02-S146, P02-S149). Boundary: the bucket and its other users are A04's (RL-05, RL-11) and A18's; the load at runtime is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED.

P02-AP07.text: - P02-AP07 — A `ZoneSet`'s age is not its candles' age: the zone cache ages from the `put`, while the warmer's fetcher serves candles for up to its own TTL, so at the committed values a set reported as at most about 1500 s old can rest on candles about 3000 s old, and about 3600 s at the extreme; the set records neither the candles' age nor the intervals used (P02-S063, P02-S065, P02-S070). Boundary: the readers are P04's diverter and A11's structure exit, which cannot see either. No source states a maximum age for the data behind a divert or a structure stop.

P02-AP08.text: - P02-AP08 — Partial and empty results stored like complete ones, and two treatments of a missing daily series: `warm` stores whatever non-empty subset of the intervals came back, and an empty zone set, for which it returns `True` while its docstring says "Returns True if zones were cached" (P02-S086); `scored_zones_from_candles` takes the prior-day levels and volume nodes from the first intraday series when the daily one is missing, while `build_anchor_payload` gives an empty `prior_day` in the same case (P02-S050, P02-S060); nothing records which series was used. Boundary: the effect on HIGH zones is P01's (P01-S079 (c)); the readers' use is P04's and A11's.

P02-AP09.text: - P02-AP09 — The prior day is chosen by list position: `prior_day_levels` uses `daily[-2]` whatever the dates, which is the previous trading day only when the series ends with a candle for today, and otherwise the day before; a one-candle series gives that candle, and a descending or duplicated series other candles (P02-S048). Whether the broker included a candle for today is UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A05 HA-04); the test states the today-candle case only (P02-S152); no source states which day was meant.

P02-AP10.text: - P02-AP10 — The warmer's queue size, idle sleep and enable flag are fixed in the code (A02 K-23's A08 side): `main.py` passes none of them, no configuration key reaches them, and the configurable `sr_detector.max_queue` governs only the V1 detector's queue (P02-S075, P02-S076, P02-S102). P02-AP11.text: - P02-AP11 — The warmer's lifecycle edges: a failure of the V2 wiring before `main.py` L3796 with the structure exit off leaves a warmer that the processor holds but that is never started, whose queue fills and then drops each new symbol with a WARNING (P02-S078); `stop` joins for 2.0 s without checking the outcome, lets a running warm finish later (by then a limiter wait has already been aborted by the shutdown event, while a broker call is not interrupted; P02-S089, added in the check), does not drain the queue and leaves `enqueue` accepting symbols, and a later `start` could run a second worker (P02-S088, P02-S089); `start` is not locked (P02-S077). P02-AP12.text: - P02-AP12 — The dedup covers only queued symbols, and each signal triggers a warm: a symbol can be queued again while it is warmed; a fresh `ZoneSet` does not prevent a new warm on each new signal; a symbol accepted while no worker runs is never removed from `_pending` (P02-S081). No source states whether a signal for a symbol with fresh zones was meant to trigger a warm.

P02-AP13.text: - P02-AP13 — Concurrency inside the fetcher: no single-flight (two threads that miss on one key both fetch), no serialization of closure calls on one object or across objects, and a cache hit returns the shared, mutable list object (P02-S033, P02-S034). P02-R1.text: - P02-R1 (P02-AP06, P02-AP05) — In the legacy code, the zone warmer (built only when the retest or the structure-exit switch is on; both are off in the committed file) keeps refreshing a stock's support and resistance zones, once it has worked on that stock, about every 25 minutes (at the file's settings) for as long as the program runs, after the market closes as well, and it never drops a stock from its list; a stock whose refresh gets no price data at all is retried about every 2 seconds (wording made precise in the check). Was the refreshing meant to stop at some point? A: no, refreshing for as long as the program ran was intended; B: it was meant to stop at the market close; C: it was meant to stop once the stock had no live signal or trade; D: not sure; Other.

If the broker sent no candle for today (for example before the market opened), the code would take the day before that. Which day did you intend? A: always the last fully completed trading day; B: the second-to-last candle, as coded; C: not sure; Other.

P03-S053.text: - P03-S053 INTERPRETATION (what the "breakout candle" is; from P03-S052, P03-S043, P01-S094): with the committed timeframes the breakout candle is the last element of the 30-minute list (the 60-minute list if the 30-minute interval failed, the daily list if both failed); "last" is list position, which is the newest candle only if the fetched rows are in ascending time (nothing sorts them, P01-S021; A05 CM-05); the average is the arithmetic mean of the volumes of up to 20 candles before it (fewer when the list is shorter; the last candle's own volume when it is alone). The breakout candle is not tied to the candidate: it is the last candle the fetch returned at processing time, whether or not it contains the placement time, and it can be a candle still forming (P03-S057; A05 HA-04). Volumes are `Candle.volume` integers, 0 where the broker gave none (P01-S018).

P03-S064.label: INTERPRETATION
P03-S064.text: - P03-S064 INTERPRETATION (what "nearest" means; from P03-S063, P01-S004 (b), P01-S093): the nearest resistance is the resistance zone whose centre is closest to the entry among those reaching up to or above the entry (a zone that contains the entry qualifies); only when no resistance reaches the entry does it fall back to all resistances, so the recorded "nearest resistance" can lie wholly below the entry. The mirror holds for supports (the fallback can give a support wholly above the entry). The choice ignores confidence (LOW zones included) and distance limits; on equal distances `min` keeps the first zone in list order, which is ascending centre.

INTERPRETATION: both are percentages of the entry price, measured to the zone's centre, not to its nearer edge; they are positive when the resistance is above and the support below the entry, and negative in the fallback cases of P03-S064. The column comments (`core/schema.sql` L1271 to L1272) state no unit or sign.

Short mirrors."): `pad = zone.center * (proximity_pct / 100.0)`; long: `(zone.band_low - pad) <= entry <= zone.band_high`; short: `zone.band_low <= entry <= (zone.band_high + pad)`.

P03-S068.label: INTERPRETATION
P03-S068.text: - P03-S068 INTERPRETATION (the "into" rule; from P03-S066, P03-S067): a long entry is "into" resistance when it lies inside the nearest resistance's band or below its bottom by at most `entry_proximity_pct` per cent of the band's centre (1 per cent committed, so 5.0 for a zone centred at 500), both ends inclusive; an entry above the band's top is never "into" it. Only the one nearest resistance is tested: another HIGH zone that also satisfies the test is not looked at. The pad is one-sided (below for a long, above for a short), unlike `ScoredZone.contains`, which widens both sides (P01-S027; the same code as `Zone.contains`, P01-S024).

P03-S069.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P03-S069.text: - P03-S069 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the confidence rule; from L82 to L86 and L96 to L100): when the entry is "into" the nearest zone, the flag is `BUYING_INTO_RESISTANCE` (or `SELLING_INTO_SUPPORT`) only for a zone whose `confidence` is exactly `"HIGH"`; for `"MEDIUM"` or `"LOW"` it is `LOW_CONFIDENCE_STRUCTURE`. INTERPRETATION: `LOW_CONFIDENCE_STRUCTURE` therefore means "the entry is into the nearest zone, and that zone is not HIGH"; when the entry is into no zone, no confidence flag is raised, whatever the confidences are.

None if there is no such zone."): long: among the zones with `band_high <= entry`, the one with the greatest `band_high`; short: among the zones with `band_low >= entry`, the one with the smallest `band_low`; `None` if there is none. P03-S071.text: - P03-S071 FACT (`_breakout_flags`, L149 to L175): returns if the zone or the breakout context is `None` (L157 to L158); `width = max(zone.band_high - zone.band_low, 1e-9)` (L159); long: `cleared = last_close > band_high`, `poke_fail = last_high > band_high and last_close <= band_high`, `weak = cleared and (last_close - band_high) < weak_breakout_frac * width` (L161 to L165); short: `cleared = last_close < band_low`, `poke_fail = last_low < band_low and last_close >= band_low`, `weak = cleared and (band_low - last_close) < weak_breakout_frac * width` (L166 to L170); `any_breakout = cleared or poke_fail`; append `"WEAK_BREAKOUT"` if `weak or poke_fail` (L172 to L173); append `"NO_VOLUME_CONFIRMATION"` if `any_breakout and avg_volume > 0 and last_volume < volume_surge_mult * avg_volume` (L174 to L175).

P03-S072.label: INTERPRETATION
P03-S072.text: - P03-S072 INTERPRETATION (what the breakout rules test; from P03-S070, P03-S071, P03-S053): (a) the "broken" zone is chosen against the entry, any confidence, at any distance below it (a long's broken resistance can lie far below the entry); (b) `cleared` compares the breakout candle's close (the last 30-minute candle, P03-S053) with that zone's top, and nothing requires that candle, or any recent candle, to have crossed the zone: for a long whose last close is above the nearest lower resistance, a "breakout" is counted even if the price has been above that zone for weeks; (c) `WEAK_BREAKOUT` is a close above the top by less than a quarter of the zone's width (loader `weak_breakout_frac` 0.25), or a candle whose high passed the top while its close did not; for a zone of zero width the floor `1e-9` leaves in practice only the poke-and-fail case (a close above the top by less than 2.5e-10 being the only other) (P01-AP04 records zero-width zones); (d) `NO_VOLUME_CONFIRMATION` is a breakout of either kind with the candle's volume below 1.5 times the average of the preceding candles (the candle's own volume when it is the only one in the list, P03-S052, so that a lone candle with a positive volume always gets the flag on a breakout); it is never raised when the average is 0 (for example when every volume defaulted to 0 in `Candle.from_kite`, P01-S018), and a breakout candle still forming carries only its volume so far (P03-S053); (e) both flags can be raised together; (f) no breakout flag is possible when the fetch returned none of `30minute`, `60minute` and `day` (configured timeframes `15minute` and `5minute` only), because the breakout context is then `None` (P03-S052).

P03-S073.label: FACT
P03-S073.text: - P03-S073 FACT (order and de-duplication, L104 to L107): `seen` and `ordered = [f for f in flags if not (f in seen or seen.add(f))]` keep the first occurrence of each flag in order; the result's `flags` is `tuple(ordered)`. The possible order is: the "into" flag (`BUYING_INTO_RESISTANCE`, `SELLING_INTO_SUPPORT` or `LOW_CONFIDENCE_STRUCTURE`), then `WEAK_BREAKOUT`, then `NO_VOLUME_CONFIRMATION`; `NO_CLEAR_STRUCTURE` only alone (L74 to L76).

P03-S074.label: INTERPRETATION
P03-S074.text: - P03-S074 INTERPRETATION (the combinations; from P03-S066 to P03-S073): each call appends each flag at most once (one "into" flag at most; each breakout flag at most once), so the de-duplication changes nothing at the baseline. The zone tested for "into" (the nearest resistance) and the "broken" zone can be the same zone in two cases: in the fallback of P03-S064 (no resistance reaches the entry), where the "into" test fails because the zone's top is below the entry, so only breakout flags can come from that zone; and when the entry equals that zone's top exactly (`band_high == entry` meets both `>=` and `<=`), where a long can carry an "into" flag (`BUYING_INTO_RESISTANCE` or `LOW_CONFIDENCE_STRUCTURE`) together with the breakout flags of that same zone. Otherwise they are different zones (the first reaches above the entry, the second lies below it); the mirror holds for a short. A candidate with zones but no flag gets an empty tuple and `structure_status` `OK` (P03-S047).

P03-S075.label: FACT
P03-S075.text: - P03-S075 FACT (`_retest_for_long`, L178 to L181; comment "Wait for a break above and a retest of the zone from above (res→support)"): `sl = zone.band_low * (1.0 - params.retest_sl_buffer_pct / 100.0)`; returns `RetestProposal(would_wait=True, entry=zone.band_high, sl=sl)`. `_retest_for_short` (L184 to L186): `sl = zone.band_high * (1.0 + params.retest_sl_buffer_pct / 100.0)`; returns `RetestProposal(would_wait=True, entry=zone.band_low, sl=sl)`. `RetestProposal` is `sr_detector/models.py` L156 to L161 (`would_wait=False`, `entry=None`, `sl=None` by default; docstring "V1 logs the PROPOSAL only — the hypothetical outcome is a later EOD step"; P01-S033).

P03-S076.label: INTERPRETATION
P03-S076.text: - P03-S076 INTERPRETATION (what the proposal is; from P03-S066, P03-S075, P03-S081): a proposal exists only when `BUYING_INTO_RESISTANCE` or `SELLING_INTO_SUPPORT` is flagged, that is, for an entry into a HIGH zone; for a long it proposes an entry at the zone's top (a retest after a break above) and a stop `retest_sl_buffer_pct` per cent (loader 0.3; the key is not in the committed file) below the zone's bottom; for a short the mirror. It is written to the row's `would_wait_for_retest` (1 or 0), `proposed_retest_entry` and `proposed_retest_sl` (P03-S081) and is used by nothing else: no non-test code outside `flags.py` and `detector.py` names `RetestProposal`, `compute_flags_and_retest` or the proposal's fields, and no code reads the three proposal columns back (`git grep` of the names and of the three column names, with the four exclusions, outside `tests/` and `docs/`: only `flags.py`, `detector.py`, `models.py`, the schema, the store's column tuple and the V2 diverter's own write). P03-S079.label: INTERPRETATION
P03-S079.text: - P03-S079 INTERPRETATION (edge inputs; from L61 to L186 and P01-S005): an `intended_entry` of 0.0 gives `None` distances but the flags are still computed (the pads use the zone centre); a NaN entry makes every comparison false, so no "into" flag, no broken zone and no breakout flag arise, while `_nearest` still returns a zone (the `min` key is NaN for every zone, so the first zone is returned, P01-S133) and the distances are NaN; a direction other than `LONG` or `BUY` (including `SELL`, empty text or a misspelling) takes the short branch (P01-S031). P03-S168.text: - P03-S168 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A05 HA-04; P07-S047; record: UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED with a MATCH part, OPEN, no treatment; Owner "A08 (the V1 detector, the retest monitor, the fetcher's cache)"; question: whether the V1 detector, the zone warmer and the retest monitor can use a last candle that is still forming, and whether any A08 code states or applies a rule for it): FACT: no A08 file states or applies a rule for a still-forming last candle (case-insensitive search of the sixteen A08 paths for `forming`, `partial`, `incomplete`, `as_of`, `asof`, `truncat`, `closed candle`, `still.open`, `lookahead`: the only hits are the backfill docstring's "still-open trade" and the export script's own `as_of` clock, part P05). The V1 detector fetches windows that end at the clock time of processing and uses the lists as returned: its zones are computed on them (P01-S096: a forming bar cannot be a pivot but can decide its neighbours and adds its partial volume to the profile) and its breakout candle is the last element of the 30-minute list (P03-S043, P03-S052, P03-S053, P03-S057). Within the fetcher's 1800 s cache time a list whose last candle was incomplete is served again (part P02, HA-06; A05 HA-04 records the same). The zone warmer's `warm` fetches the structure intervals the same way and truncates nothing (`sr_detector/zone_warmer.py` L129 to L139; part P02); the retest monitor keeps the one-minute candles from the divert time onwards and drops none at the end (`screening/retest_monitor.py` L216 to L225; part P04). UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the broker's answers of the legacy period included a forming candle (the vendor page does not say, P01-S004 (a)), and so whether any V1 row was computed on one. Whether the V1 detector was meant to use an incomplete last candle is the history question of entry A05-29 (P03-S172), not answered here.

So it waits neither for a queue slot nor for the analysis, and it raises nothing for a `Candidate`, the only type its production callers pass (an object without `symbol` would raise in the `Full` handler, P03-S040); on a full queue or an unexpected error it makes one log call on the caller's thread (P03-S039). These code facts are consistent with the MATCH as recorded; the classification is A06's and is not reopened here. Its indirect effects through shared resources (the broker client and limiter, the database's write lock, interpreter time) are recorded in P03-S105 to P03-S107 and are outside "the enqueue" that the MATCH row names.

P03-AP01.text: - P03-AP01 — Indirect effects of the observer on the order path: the texts say the observer "NEVER blocks/delays placement and NEVER raises into the pipeline"; by its own code it is reached only after the placement and the `PROCESSED` write, hands off without waiting for a queue slot or the analysis, raises nothing for a `Candidate` and writes nothing that the order path reads (P03-S101 to P03-S104, P03-S111); its worker shares with the order path the live broker client and the process's rate limiter, the database's single write lock (one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` insert with a `synchronous = FULL` commit per row), interpreter time, the instrument cache and the logging, and no text states an intent or a bound for these (P03-S105 to P03-S107, P03-S193, P03-S217). Boundary: A01 and A04 for the client and the limiter (A01 C38a, A04 RL-05 and RL-11, primary part P02; A01 B-11, primary part P06), A03 for the store's locking, A05 and A15 for the instrument cache and the logging.

P03-AP02.text: - P03-AP02 — As of when the V1 evidence is computed (A05 HA-04's A08 side): the stated question is whether buying into resistance can be detected "before the outcome is known", but each analysis fetches windows that end when the worker reaches the candidate, after any queue wait and with cached lists up to 1800 s old, and nothing truncates the candles to the placement-time stamp or drops a still-forming last candle; a row can therefore rest partly on price action after the entry (P03-S043, P03-S053, P03-S057, P03-S168, P03-S194). Whether the broker returned forming candles is UNKNOWN (P03-U03).

P03-AP03.text: - P03-AP03 — What the breakout flags measure: the "breakout candle" is the last element of the 30-minute list at processing time, not a candle tied to the entry; the "broken" zone is the nearest lower resistance (or upper support) at any distance and of any confidence; a "breakout" is counted whenever the last close is beyond that zone's edge, however long the price has been there and without any candle having crossed it, and also when the last candle's high (for a short, its low) passed the edge while its close did not; `NO_VOLUME_CONFIRMATION` is not possible when the average volume is 0, is always raised on a breakout when the list holds a single candle with a positive volume, and compares a possibly partial last candle's volume with full candles (P03-S052, P03-S053, P03-S070 to P03-S072, P03-S184). Against the docstring's "breakout candle lacks follow-through" and "breakout without a volume surge" (P03-S014).

P03-AP04.text: - P03-AP04 — The flag table and the committed comment against the code: `BUYING_INTO_RESISTANCE` and its mirror test only the nearest zone with a one-sided pad; `LOW_CONFIDENCE_STRUCTURE` requires the entry to be "into" the nearest zone; `WEAK_BREAKOUT` includes a poke-and-fail; `NO_CLEAR_STRUCTURE` is raised only when no zone exists at all, a LOW zone counting as structure, and is also the only flag of a `FETCH_FAILED` row; the comment "entry within this % of a HIGH zone" (`config/system_config.yaml` L517) describes a pad the code applies to the nearest zone of any confidence; `PATHS.md` L418 omits `SELLING_INTO_SUPPORT` (P03-S014, P03-S044, P03-S048, P03-S066 to P03-S069, P03-S080, P03-S196, P03-S203).

P03-AP05.text: - P03-AP05 — Placed trades that leave no row: the schema says "One row per PLACED candidate observed by the async, non-gating S&R detector" (`core/schema.sql` L1248); a placement leaves no row when its `place()` call timed out ambiguously (the signal is marked `TIMEOUT` and `_sr_observe` is never called, even if the recovery later adopts the trade) or when the `PROCESSED` write or the seam's own `Candidate` build raises (P03-S215); and a candidate handed to the observer leaves no row when the queue is full (one WARNING), when it is still queued at `stop` or at any other end of the process, or is cut off by the interpreter's exit (no log line), when the analysis raises (one ERROR) or when the insert fails, a NULL `created_at` after a clock failure included (one ERROR); nothing in the table records these gaps (P03-S033, P03-S038, P03-S055, P03-S086, P03-S092, P03-S215, P03-S216). Boundary: A06 (and A10 for the recovery) for the cases before the hand-off.

P03-AP06.text: - P03-AP06 — "A later run picks it up" (A03 U-25's A08 side; A07 XS-12): every run selects only its date's rows and the declared 15:58 run passes no date, so a row skipped as open is revisited only by a run given that date (P03-S115, P03-S124, P03-S135, P03-S167). The finding is A03's U-25; this point adds the guard's effect on manual runs (P03-AP07).

P04-S014.label: HISTORICAL
P04-S014.text: - P04-S014 HISTORICAL (declared purpose of `retest_confirm.py`, module docstring L1 to L32): "The WAIT_FOR_RETEST confirmation state machine — PURE and unit-testable. No candle patterns / indicator names; only "broke + touched + strong close". Given the matched zone band + the 1m candles since divert + elapsed time, it returns the resulting state. SYMMETRIC: the same fold drives both sides; only the directional predicates flip (LONG = above resistance, SHORT = below support)." Design (L12 to L18): "Deterministic FOLD from WAIT_BREAKOUT over the candles (chronological). This is idempotent and restart-safe: the state is a pure function of (zone, direction, candles-since-divert, elapsed). The monitor persists the result as a snapshot but recomputes it every poll, so re-seeing candles never mis-advances." The state machine (L20 to L31) is quoted with the code in section 3 and compared with it in section 12.

P04-S015.label: HISTORICAL
P04-S015.text: - P04-S015 HISTORICAL (declared purpose of `retest_monitor.py`, module docstring L1 to L14): "The WAIT_FOR_RETEST monitor. Holds candidates DIVERTED by the pre-placement check (a LONG entry inside a HIGH resistance zone) and, on a daemon poll thread, fetches fresh 1m candles per parked symbol and advances the pure retest_confirm state machine: CONFIRMED → hand to signal_processor.continue_from_retest (reserve+MARKET). REJECT (timeout / break-down) → clear (no capital was held). Restart-safe like EntryGate: persists to retest_state, rehydrates on boot, deletes the row atomically on release. P04-S025.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S025.text: - P04-S025 INTERPRETATION (the price rules in words; from P04-S024): LONG: a break is a one-minute close strictly above `band_high × (1 + m/100)`, with `m` = `breakout_margin_pct` (at the committed 0.0, any close above the band's top); the wrong-way reject is a close strictly below `band_low × (1 − a/100)`, with `a` = `max_away_pct` (at the committed 1.0, a close more than 1 % below the band's bottom). SHORT: a break is a close strictly below `band_low × (1 − m/100)`; the wrong-way reject is a close strictly above `band_high × (1 + a/100)` (at the committed 1.0, more than 1 % above the band's top). Both percentages are applied multiplicatively to the band edge they test, not to the band's width or centre (unlike `contains`, which pads by a percentage of the centre, P01-S024); both are percentages, divided by 100 (A02 K-21's A08 side, section 11). Only closes count for the break and the reject: a high or low beyond a level does not.

P04-S027.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S027.text: - P04-S027 INTERPRETATION (the transitions; from P04-S026): (a) a candle makes at most one transition (an `if`/`elif` chain), so the breaking candle cannot also be the touch and the touching candle cannot also confirm: a confirmation needs at least three candles (break, touch, confirming break); (b) there is no backward transition: in `WAIT_RETEST` a candle that does not touch leaves the state as it is, and in `WAIT_CONFIRM` a candle that is not a strong break leaves it there, however far the price moves away, until the timeout or a wrong-way reject; (c) in `WAIT_BREAKOUT` a candle inside the band has no effect (the entry was inside the padded zone at the divert, section 4, so the first candles may well be); (d) the touch is the same test for both sides: the candle's range overlaps the unpadded band, both edges inclusive, with no margin or buffer; (e) the wrong-way test runs before the state step on every candle, so a close past the reject level ends the fold with `REJECT` in any state, after a break or a touch too; (f) a terminal result ends the fold and later candles are not examined. LONG and SHORT differ only in the predicates of P04-S024 and the polarity of `_strong_close`.

P04-S030.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S030.text: - P04-S030 INTERPRETATION (what "strong" means; from P04-S029, with the committed `confirm_strong_close_frac: 0.6`): LONG: the close must be at least 60 % of the way from the low to the high, that is, in the top 40 % of the range; SHORT: the close must be at least 60 % of the way down from the high, in the bottom 40 % of the range. A larger value is stricter; a value at or below 0 makes every bar with a positive range strong, and a value above 1 makes none strong. The comments' wording ("UPPER frac", "the strong 60%") is compared with this in section 12. Zero range (L134 to L135): a flat bar whose close equals its high and low is strong for both sides, so in `WAIT_CONFIRM` a flat one-minute bar whose close is past the break level confirms whatever the fraction is; a malformed bar with `high < low` takes the same branch. A NaN in the high, low or close gives a NaN range and position, both comparisons false, so not strong; an infinite high or low gives a position of 0 or NaN, not strong unless the fraction is at or below 0 (P04-S006).

P04-S031.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S031.text: - P04-S031 INTERPRETATION (NaN and infinite candle values in the fold; P04-S006): a NaN close neither breaks nor fails (every comparison is false), so it changes nothing; a NaN low or high makes the touch false. A positive infinite close breaks on the long side (and is not a wrong-way close) and is a wrong-way close (`reclaim_up`) on the short side; a negative infinite close is the mirror. `evaluate` validates no candle value, and `Candle.from_kite` passes NaN and infinite prices through (P01-S017).

A negative `max_away_pct` moves the reject level to the other side of the band edge (for a long, above `band_low`), so closes inside the band would reject; a negative `breakout_margin_pct` moves the break level inside the band; a `confirm_strong_close_frac` outside 0 to 1 acts as in P04-S030. The loader accepts any float for these keys (P04-S019); the committed values (1.0, 0.0, 0.6) are inside the ranges the comments describe.

P04-S033.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S033.text: - P04-S033 INTERPRETATION ("pure, idempotent and restart-safe", L12 to L18): `evaluate` is a pure function of its arguments (no clock, no state, P04-S012), so the same arguments give the same result, as the tests state (`tests/unit/test_sr_v2_retest_confirm.py` L100 to L102, L169 to L171). INTERPRETATION: (a) at the committed `near_zone_buffer_pct: 0.3`, an entry inside the band or up to 0.3 % of the centre beyond either edge matches; (b) the confidence test is exact equality with the configured value, so a zone of a higher class does not match a lower setting (with `MEDIUM` configured, a `HIGH` zone would not divert), as the loader comment "only this zone confidence diverts" (L1202) states; (c) the nearest centre wins, and among equal distances the first in the list (P04-S005 (c)), the list being in ascending centre order (P02-S052; P01-S070); (d) a NaN or infinite entry price matches no zone, every comparison being false (P04-S006), so the signal is not diverted; (e) only the side's list is read: a long entry inside a HIGH support zone, or a short entry inside a HIGH resistance zone, is not diverted (as the tests state, `tests/unit/test_sr_v2_divert.py` L99 to L103, L165 to L169).

P04-S040.text: - P04-S040 FACT and INTERPRETATION (cache misses and stale zones; `ZoneCache` and `ZoneWarmer` are part P02's): FACT: `ZoneCache.get` returns `None` for a symbol never warmed and for an entry older than its TTL, without removing it (P02-S066), and the diverter then returns `False` (L335 to L336; P02-S072). INTERPRETATION: (a) the diverter neither fetches nor asks for a warm; a symbol is warmed only after A06's `_warm_zones` enqueues it on the dispatcher thread, just before the signal is handed to a worker (P02-S080, P02-S159), and the warm runs on the warmer's thread; so whether the first signal of a symbol in a process can be diverted depends on whether that warm finished before the worker reached L1042, a timing race whose outcomes in production are UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED; (b) a hit can be up to the zone TTL old (committed 1800 s) and built from candles up to the fetcher's TTL older still, which the diverter cannot see (P02-S070, P02-S072); (c) a hit whose tuples are empty (a warm that found no zones, P02-S086) matches nothing; (d) an exception from `get` (a clock failure in the cache, P02-S066) reaches the `except` at L376 with `divert_committed` false, so the signal goes to normal placement.

INTERPRETATION: (a) only a signal that would itself divert is dropped; a later signal for an already-parked symbol whose entry matches no zone on its side (or whose symbol misses the cache) returns `False` and goes to normal placement while the earlier candidate stays parked and can still resume; (b) a short signal into a HIGH support zone of a symbol whose long candidate is parked is dropped as `REJECTED_RETEST_DUP`; (c) the dropped signal gets no parking and no `sr_detector_results` row; its status is its only record. FACT: no lock spans the `has_symbol` call (L347) and the later `register` (L371), each taking the monitor's lock on its own (L144, L95); HISTORICAL (comment L329 to L331, commit `b3a5c949260388f51ab74a592cd9d832ee91c928`): "Concurrent same-symbol signals are already serialized upstream by the receiver's atomic _claim_in_flight (M-1/FIX-011), so this method never runs twice for one symbol in parallel." Under a clock of the same form as `added_at` it would be evaluated on the candles since the divert (a two-day window covers a same-day restart) and rejected `"timeout"` if the stop outlasted the timeout; at the committed wiring its evaluation raises (P04-S070) and it stays parked. A row whose release failed (P04-S072) is restored although its signal was already handed to `continue_from_retest`; its candles since the divert still show the confirmation, so under a working clock it would be confirmed again and `on_confirm` called a second time for the same signal, whose status is by then whatever A06's resumption wrote (A06 EV-11 and EV-01 record that the resumption checks no current status; what it then does is A06's).

P04-S087.text: - P04-S087 INTERPRETATION (what the end-of-day clear leaves; from P04-S085, P04-S086, P04-S059 and P04-S069): memory and the table are emptied (if the store call succeeds); each cleared signal keeps its last status, `RETEST_WAITING` (or the screener's `PASSED` if that write had failed), and no terminal status records the end of its parking; its divert row in `sr_detector_results` stays; such signals are outside the prune predicate (P04-S059) and stay in `signals`. If the store call fails, memory is cleared but the rows stay and are restored at the next boot. The number reported is the in-memory count, not the rows deleted. A poll that took its snapshot before the clear can still evaluate a cleared candidate and, on a terminal result, call the release (its `DELETE` then matches no row, while its `UPDATE` of `signals` still writes `RETEST_CONFIRMED` or `RETEST_REJECTED_*`) and, on a confirmation, the callback, whose own entry-window check (A06's, `signals/signal_processor.py` L2400, named only) is not audited here; an in-progress state change of a cleared candidate is not written back to memory (the presence test, L198), while `update_retest_state` is still called and matches no row.

P04-S090.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S090.text: - P04-S090 INTERPRETATION (a shutdown with a poll in progress; from P04-S089, P04-S064, P04-S005 (c) and P02-S089): the stop flag is read only between polls; a poll in progress, a fetch or a callback inside `continue_from_retest`, is not interrupted, and `join` returns after 2.0 s without it; the daemon thread then finishes that poll, so a resumption can still size, reserve and place after `stop` has returned (subject to A06's own stop-event test before placement, `signals/signal_processor.py` L2524 to L2528, named only), or it is stopped abruptly when the interpreter exits. Because `_shutdown` sets the shutdown event first, a limiter wait on the monitor's thread aborts and the fetcher logs it as "historical_data failed", so a fetch during shutdown gives no candles (P02-S089). The processor is stopped (L1690) before the monitor (L1733), so a confirmation in that interval is handed to a processor that has stopped its own workers; A06 EV-11 records that the processor's `stop()` does not wait for the retest thread. The parked rows stay in the table for the next boot. A `start` after a timed-out `stop` would start a second thread beside the first, `_worker` having been set to `None`; `main.py` makes no such call.

P04-S103.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P04-S103.text: - P04-S103 FACT and INTERPRETATION (what A08 receives back): FACT: nothing. The function is annotated `-> None` and returns `None` on every route: at the end of its `try`, on the route without a placer (L2512) and on the ambiguous placement time-out (L2577); the monitor discards the value (L187). Its handlers catch `_PipelineReject` (L2594 to L2614) and every other `Exception` (L2616 to L2628), and its `finally` adjusts counters (L2630 to L2640); an exception reaches the monitor only if it is raised inside a handler or the `finally` (a status write in a handler, L2598 or L2620, for example) or derives from `BaseException` only, and the monitor then logs ERROR "retest_monitor: continue_from_retest raised for <signal ID>: <exception>" and goes on (L188 to L190). The signal's status after the handoff is written by the function itself, through `update_signal_status`: `PROCESSING` (L2393), `RESERVED` (L2501), `PROCESSED_NO_PLACER` (L2509), `TIMEOUT` with the error text (L2573 to L2575), `PROCESSED` (L2583), `REJECTED_<check>` with the reason (L2598; for the retest-specific check, `REJECTED_RETEST_BAD_STRUCTURE`) or `PLACEMENT_FAILED` with the exception text (L2620). INTERPRETATION: A08 learns nothing of the outcome: the candidate is already released with `RETEST_CONFIRMED` before the call (P04-S073), the monitor keeps no record of the result and does not retry, and a rejection inside the resumption ends the signal without parking it again; the only traces of the outcome are the signal's later status and the rows the resumption and its callees write.

P04-S108.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S108.text: - P04-S108 INTERPRETATION (the interleavings the code allows; from P04-S107 and sections 4 to 7): (a) the diverter's duplicate test and its `register` are separate critical sections (P04-S041); (b) a poll's snapshot and `clear_all` (P04-S087); (c) a `register` during a poll: the new candidate is first evaluated at the next poll (P04-S065); (d) a confirmation's `_release` and a later divert of the same symbol: the symbol is free as soon as the release has removed it from memory, before the resumption runs, so a new in-zone signal of the same symbol can be parked while, or after, the first is resumed and placed; whether a second entry on that symbol is then refused is A06's and A09's (the one-trade-per-symbol-direction check, `signals/signal_processor.py` L2478, named only); (e) `rehydrate` cannot overlap a poll, running before `start` (L3795, L3797), and runs before the processor's start (L3974), so no divert can interleave with it.
P04-S108.sec: 9. Threads, locks, clocks and failure behaviour (summary)

P04-S110.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S110.text: - P04-S110 INTERPRETATION (what the clocks mean; A06 WA-06's A08 side): the retest clock starts at the divert, read from the trading process's wall clock, and is not the signal's scan or receipt time: no A08 file reads `triggered_at` (search of the sixteen A08 paths), and the `ParkedCandidate` carries no trigger time (P04-S048). The elapsed time and the timeout are wall-clock and calendar time: a backward step of the system clock would lengthen a wait and a forward step shorten it (once the subtraction works); the candle filter compares IST wall-clock digits (P04-S066); the stored times drop the offset (P04-S051). At the committed wiring the elapsed time cannot be computed at all (P04-S070).
P04-S110.sec: 9. Threads, locks, clocks and failure behaviour (summary)

P04-S111.label: FACT
P04-S111.text: - P04-S111 FACT (the direction and side tests on the V2 path): `_process_one` maps the strategy direction to the side with `_dir in ("LONG", "BUY")` (`signals/signal_processor.py` L1035, A06's); the diverter selects the zone list by `side == "BUY"` or `side == "SELL"` and refuses any other side (L321 to L324); the audit row decides its columns by `parked.direction in ("LONG", "BUY")` (L399); `evaluate` decides the fold's side by `_is_long`, case-insensitive and stripped (L50 to L51, L92); `continue_from_retest` decides its side and stop by `parked.direction in ("LONG", "BUY")` (L2435). They agree for the two directions the strategy schema admits (P04-S105).

P04-S112.label: FACT
P04-S112.text:
- P04-S112 FACT (failure behaviour, summary; each row cites the statements that establish it):
| Condition | What the V2 code does | Statements |
|---|---|---|
| switch off (committed) | nothing is built; the divert test is false | P04-S016 |
| zone cache miss, expired entry, or `get` raising | not diverted; normal placement | P04-S040 |
| no zone of the required confidence on the side contains the entry (NaN or infinite entry included) | not diverted | P04-S039 |
| symbol already parked and the entry in a zone | `REJECTED_RETEST_DUP`; the signal is dropped | P04-S041, P04-S044 |
| `register`'s insert fails | parked in memory only; `RETEST_WAITING`; lost at a restart | P04-S074 |
| the `RETEST_WAITING` write fails | parked; the status stays as the screener left it; no audit row; `True` returned | P04-S044 |
| the audit write fails | ERROR; parked | P04-S045 |
| the one-minute fetch fails or is empty | the fold runs on no candles: in progress (the stored state can move back) or a timeout | P04-S066, P04-S076 |
| the elapsed time at the committed wiring (aware clock, naive `added_at`) | `TypeError` at every evaluation; ERROR "evaluate failed"; the candidate stays parked and is fetched at every poll | P04-S070 |
| `evaluate` or the filter raises (a malformed candle) | ERROR "evaluate failed"; the candidate stays | P04-S065 |
| `update_retest_state` fails | ERROR; memory updated, the row not | P04-S069 |
| the release's store call fails | memory entry gone; row and old status stay; on a confirmation the callback still runs | P04-S072 |
| the callback raises out of its handlers | ERROR "continue_from_retest raised"; the poll goes on | P04-S073, P04-S103 |
| the table read at boot fails | ERROR; nothing restored; rows stay | P04-S079 |
| a row cannot be converted | ERROR; skipped in memory; left in the table | P04-S079, P04-S081 |
| the end-of-day store clear fails | memory cleared; rows stay and are restored at the next boot | P04-S085, P04-S087 |
| `stop` during a poll | 2.0 s join; the poll finishes on the daemon thread or is cut at exit | P04-S090 |
| a thread start fails in the wiring block | the diverter stays bound; the monitor may not poll; parked candidates wait for the end-of-day clear | P04-S091 |
P04-S112.sec: 9. Threads, locks, clocks and failure behaviour (summary)

P04-S113.label: INTERPRETATION
P04-S113.text: - P04-S113 INTERPRETATION (from P04-S112): A08's V2 code retries nothing, raises no alert and calls no notifier (neither file imports one, P04-S012, P04-S013); its failures are ERROR lines and, at the diverter, a fall-back to normal placement before the commit point or a silent hold after it. `maybe_divert` never raises an `Exception` to the processor (P04-S038), and nothing in the monitor's thread can end it except an exception deriving from `BaseException` only (P04-S064, P04-S065).

P04-S134.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P04-S134.text: - P04-S134 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A03 P-11; P07-S033; A03 AUDIT L1714 to L1726, case (5); Audit Findings Register L433: "ISSUE; FACT; INTERPRETATION"; "A03 treatment group TG2 (AGREED, 11-Nov-2026)"; "AGREED"; unchanged). Asked: which separately committed writes the divert and the release make, in which order, and what a stop between them leaves. A08 side: the divert makes, after the memory insert, three transactions in this order: the `retest_state` insert (inside `register`, L97), the `RETEST_WAITING` status (L373) and the `sr_detector_results` row (L413) (P04-S046); the release is one transaction (delete and status update together, P04-S055), preceded by the memory removal and followed by the callback (P04-S069, P04-S072); the end-of-day clear is the memory clear then one `DELETE` (P04-S085). INTERPRETATION: a stop after the insert and before the status leaves a stored candidate whose signal keeps the screener's `PASSED` and has no divert row; it is restored at the next boot (P04-S081); a stop after the status and before the audit row leaves no divert row; a stop between the release and the callback's first write (`PROCESSING`, L2393) leaves the signal at `RETEST_CONFIRMED` with no row, and nothing in A08 parks or resumes it again. Records note (section 13): P-11 cites `screening/retest_monitor.py` "L370 to L371: memory first, persistence best-effort, by stated design"; at the baseline the memory-first order is `register`'s L95 to L97 (docstring L93), while L370 to L371 are the end of the `ParkedCandidate` construction and the `register` call.

P04-S135.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P04-S135.text: - P04-S135 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A03 Q-11; P07-S034; A03 AUDIT L2039 to L2052; Audit Findings Register L446: "ISSUE; FACT; INTERPRETATION"; "A03 treatment group TG2 (AGREED, 11-Nov-2026)"; "AGREED"; unchanged). Asked: what the monitor does when the release raises: its memory, the stored row, the resume call, and what a restart rehydrates. A08 side: the memory entry is already removed and is not restored; the row and the signal's old status stay; on a confirmation the callback is still called (P04-S072); a restart restores the row (P04-S081), and, under a working clock, its candles would confirm it again and `on_confirm` would run a second time for the signal (P04-S082); the per-symbol guard is lost meanwhile, so a second candidate of the same symbol can be parked (P04-S083); the end-of-day clear deletes such rows (P04-S085). At the committed wiring no candidate is evaluated at all (P04-S070), so neither the first nor a second confirmation would occur through the monitor. Records note (section 13): Q-11 cites `rehydrate` as "L117 to L132"; at the baseline the method is L118 to L136, its loop L126 to L133.

P04-S136.text: - P04-S136 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A06 WA-06; P07-S054; A06 AUDIT L1974 to L2023; Audit Findings Register L1160: "ISSUE; FACT; INTERPRETATION; HISTORICAL"; "A06 treatment group TG1 (AGREED, 19-Nov-2026)"; "AGREED"; unchanged; its Owner field names A06 only, A08 reaching it through the handoff row L2271, P07 AP-03). Asked: whether any A08 code reads the signal's `triggered_at`, and from which clock the retest clock and the observer's time come. A08 side: no A08 file reads `triggered_at` (search of the sixteen A08 paths; P04-S110); the retest clock starts at the divert, read from the diverter's clock (`time_authority.now_ist`, L368), and the `ParkedCandidate` carries no trigger time (P04-S048); the V1 observer's `ts` is set by A06's `_sr_observe` from `now_ist()` (`signals/signal_processor.py` L652; P03-S085). INTERPRETATION: a signal whose `triggered_at` lies after its receipt (WA-06's case), if diverted, is timed from its divert, not from its scan time; nothing on the V2 path depends on `triggered_at`.

P04-S137.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P04-S137.text: - P04-S137 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A06 WA-07; P07-S055; A06 AUDIT L2024 to L2074; Audit Findings Register L1161: "ISSUE; FACT; INTERPRETATION; HISTORICAL"; "A06 treatment group TG1 (AGREED, 19-Nov-2026)"; "AGREED"; unchanged; its Owner field names "A07 to A10", a range that includes A08, P07-S066). Asked: how A08 code uses the trigger price and the entry price derived from it (zone matching, the parked row, the resume), and what a NaN or infinite value would meet there. A08 side: the derived entry price is used only for the zone match (a NaN or infinite entry matches no zone, so the signal is not diverted, P04-S039 (d)), stored in the parked record and the row, and written as the divert row's `intended_entry` (P04-S045); the resumption does not read it (P04-S095). The trigger price is stored as `float(trigger_price or 0.0)` (a NaN stays NaN, `None` or 0 become 0.0; P04-S043), written to `retest_state.trigger_price`, restored from a NULL as 0.0 (P04-S052) and passed to A10 as `signal_trigger_price` and to the evidence record (P04-S099, P04-S101). INTERPRETATION, conditional: whether `_derive_prices` can give a finite entry with a NaN trigger or stop is A06's and A07's; if a parked candidate carried a NaN trigger price, then on the storage reading that A06 WA-07 records as current external context (a NaN bound as a REAL is stored as NULL; A03's to confirm), its row would hold NULL and the value would come back as 0.0 after a restart, while the in-memory value stays NaN; a NaN pre-divert stop with a finite entry would meet the `sl_price REAL NOT NULL` column (`core/schema.sql` L1321), so on that reading the insert would fail and the candidate would be parked in memory only (P04-S074).

P04-S138.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P04-S138.text: - P04-S138 FACT and INTERPRETATION (A06 EV-11; P07-S060; A06 AUDIT L4709 to L4763; Audit Findings Register L1201: "ISSUE (latent); FACT; INTERPRETATION; HISTORICAL"; "A06 treatment group TG6 (AGREED, 19-Nov-2026)"; "AGREED"; unchanged). Asked: on which thread the monitor calls `on_confirm`, what it does before the call, whether a second resumption of one signal is possible from A08's side, whether `stop()` waits for a resumption in progress, and what A08 receives back. A08 side: on its own daemon thread "sr-retest-monitor", synchronously inside the poll (P04-S073); before the call it removes the candidate from memory, releases the row with `RETEST_CONFIRMED` and logs an INFO line (P04-S069); from A08's side a second resumption needs a restart after a failed release, or a second divert of the same signal (P04-S073, P04-S082); `RetestMonitor.stop()` waits at most 2.0 s and a resumption in progress continues after it returns (P04-S089, P04-S090); A08 receives nothing back (P04-S103). The resumption's first statement, `PROCESSING` with no status check (L2393), is A06's and is named only (P04-S104).

P04-S139.label: FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED
P04-S139.text: - P04-S139 FACT, INTERPRETATION and UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (A07 SL-06; P07-S062; A07 AUDIT L866 to L879; Audit Findings Register L1314: "UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED; FACT; HISTORICAL; INTERPRETATION"; "None (UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED items receive no treatment)"; "UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED (no treatment)"; unchanged; D-41 P1: facts only). Asked: under which switches the retest path (diverter, monitor, `continue_from_retest`) is built and reachable at the committed values, and whether its use in production is established. A08 side: FACT: it is built only when `sr_detector.wait_for_retest_enabled` is true and the warmer and the cache exist (`main.py` L3423, L3769; P04-S016); at the committed `false` nothing is built, the processor's diverter stays `None`, the divert test at L1042 is false, and `continue_from_retest`, whose only caller is the monitor (L187), is not reached (P04-S094). INTERPRETATION: with the switch on, the path is built, but at the baseline wiring the monitor's elapsed-time subtraction raises at every evaluation (P04-S070), so no candidate reaches `on_confirm`, and `continue_from_retest` (with its strategy-control call at L2411) is not reached through the monitor even then, unless the monitor were given a clock of the form of `added_at`. UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the switch was ever true on a legacy machine and whether any part of the path ran; the legacy documents' statements that it did not are runtime claims, HISTORICAL (section 12).

P04-S161.label: HISTORICAL and INTERPRETATION
P04-S161.text: - P04-S161 HISTORICAL and INTERPRETATION (the state machine in `retest_confirm.py`'s docstring, L20 to L31, against the code): each stated transition is what the code does (P04-S024 to P04-S027): the break is a one-minute close past `band_high` (long) or `band_low` (short), with the margin; the retest touch is the candle's range re-entering the band; the confirmation is a new break with a strong close; the reject is an elapsed time above `timeout_sec` or a close more than `max_away_pct` the wrong way past the band, with the reasons `"break_down"` and `"reclaim_up"`. The docstring does not state that a candle makes at most one transition, that no transition goes back, that the timeout overrides a confirming list, or that the wrong-way test runs first on every candle (P04-S023, P04-S027).
P04-S161.sec: 12.1 Docstrings and comments against the code

P04-S163.label: HISTORICAL and INTERPRETATION
P04-S163.text: - P04-S163 HISTORICAL and INTERPRETATION (the strong-close wording): `_strong_close`'s docstring "LONG wants the close in the UPPER frac of the 1m range, SHORT in the LOWER frac" (L131 to L132), the module docstring "confirm close strong in UPPER frac" (L21), the committed comment "confirm close must be in the strong 60% of the 1m candle (upper=LONG / lower=SHORT)" (`config/system_config.yaml` L534) and the loader comment "close must be in the strong N of the 1m range (upper=LONG/lower=SHORT)" (`core/config_loader.py` L1205); against them, the field comment "strong close: directional close position ≥ this" (L58) and the code `pos >= frac` (L137). INTERPRETATION: read as "in the upper 60 % of the range", the first four would accept a close at 40 % of the range or higher, while the code requires 60 % or higher (the top 40 %); the field comment states the code's reading; the tests' cases (P04-S171) do not tell the two readings apart. Which was meant is not stated elsewhere (section 13; section 15).
P04-S163.sec: 12.1 Docstrings and comments against the code

P04-S182.text: - P04-S182 HISTORICAL and FACT (`git blame` of the cited lines): the clock lines L171, L219 to L223, L230 to L231, L239, L368 and L398 date from `9f56b0775163c690de977ec354176b5be5abb62c`; L399 (the audit row's direction test) from `02357130fe09fab38833e81ce59f1b0f407488bc`. P04-AP01.text: - P04-AP01 — The monitor's elapsed time at the committed wiring: `_evaluate` subtracts the naive divert time (`added_at`, made naive at L368 and restored naive by `_from_row`; field comment L40 "naive IST") from the monitor's `now_fn()` (L171), and `main.py` gives the monitor the aware `time_authority.now_ist` (L3787; `core/time_authority.py` L94 to L99); by the Python documentation that subtraction raises `TypeError`, so every evaluation fails after its fetch and, with the switch on, no candidate would be confirmed, rejected or timed out, against the docstrings' "CONFIRMED → hand to signal_processor.continue_from_retest" and "REJECT (timeout / break-down) → clear" (L9 to L10) and the timeout of `retest_confirm` (L28). The tests give the monitor a naive clock and so do not show it. Whether the switch was ever on is UNKNOWN. Sources: P04-S070, P04-S005, P04-S006, P04-S172, P04-S168.

P04-AP02.text: - P04-AP02 — The end-of-day clear writes no status: `clear_all` deletes the rows and empties memory (L107 to L116), so the cleared signals keep `RETEST_WAITING` with no final status, while the schema comment says the row is deleted "atomically on release (confirm / reject / EOD)" (`core/schema.sql` L1306 to L1307) and the store's release writes a status with the delete (`core/state_store.py` L3049 to L3059); such signals are outside the prune predicate (`scripts/eod_cleanup.py` L234 to L236). A poll whose snapshot predates the clear can still release a cleared candidate (writing `RETEST_CONFIRMED` or `RETEST_REJECTED_*` after the clear) and hand it to the resumption. Sources: P04-S085, P04-S087, P04-S059, P04-S165.

P04-AP03.text: - P04-AP03 — The duplicate guard: the comment L344 to L346 says "a symbol already parked must not spawn a 2nd MARKET entry (overlap invariant). Drop the duplicate signal rather than placing it into the zone", but the test runs only after a zone match, so a later signal of a parked symbol that matches no zone goes to normal placement while the parked candidate can still resume; the symbol is free again as soon as a confirmation's release has run, before the resumption; and the test and the `register` call are separate critical sections whose serialization the comment L329 to L331 attributes to A06's upstream claim (A06's to confirm). Sources: P04-S041, P04-S108 (d), P04-S167, P04-S181.

P04-AP04.text: - P04-AP04 — Release before resumption (A03 Q-11's A08 side; Q-11 unchanged): the comment L181 to L182 says the row is released first "so it can't be re-evaluated"; when the release's store call fails the memory entry is gone, the row and old status stay, the callback runs, and a restart restores the row, which can then be confirmed and resumed again; meanwhile the per-symbol guard is lost and a second candidate of the same symbol can be parked, so two rows of one symbol can be restored. Sources: P04-S072, P04-S082, P04-S083, P04-S135.

P04-AP05.text: - P04-AP05 — The strong-close wording against the code: the docstrings and the committed and loader comments say the close must be "in the UPPER frac" or "in the strong 60%" of the range, which read literally admits a close at 40 % of the range or above; the code and the `RetestParams` field comment require a position of at least the fraction (60 %, the top 40 % of the range). Sources: P04-S163, P04-S029, P04-S030.

P04-AP06.text: - P04-AP06 — Long-only texts after the short mirror: the monitor's docstring, two schema comments (A03's), two processor comments (A06's) and a loader comment (A02's) describe a long-only design that the code no longer has since `02357130fe09fab38833e81ce59f1b0f407488bc`. Sources: P04-S164, P04-S180.

P04-AP07.text: - P04-AP07 — Stored or declared and never used: `retest_state.sizing_inputs` ("JSON snapshot of inputs to re-size at confirm") is restored but not read by the resumption, which re-derives its inputs; `retest_state.timeout_at` ("deadline") is written and never read, the timeout in force being the monitor's current `timeout_sec` (so a changed `retest_timeout_sec` would apply to restored candidates whatever their stored deadline); `IN_PROGRESS_STATES`, `RetestResult.terminal` and `parked_count` have no non-test reader; `field` is imported and unused and `json` is imported twice (L17, L397). Sources: P04-S166, P04-S012, P04-S013, P04-S020, P04-S052, P04-S075.

P04-AP08.text: - P04-AP08 — The stored state is not monotonic: after a fetch with no candles the snapshot is written back to `WAIT_BREAKOUT` and later advanced again, against the docstring's "re-seeing candles never mis-advances"; the outcome is not affected, the state not being an input. Sources: P04-S076, P04-S162.

P04-AP09.text: - P04-AP09 — Rehydration has no date and no status filter: every row is restored whatever its day or its signal's status, while the end-of-day comment intends that none "survive into the next session" (`orders/eod_squareoff.py` L349 to L350) and A18's analogous PB-01 stage, which calls itself "the direct analog" of `RetestMonitor`, states an anti-rehydration rule that loads "ONLY today's rows" (`v3_chain/pb01_entry.py` L6 to L7, L17 to L19). Sources: P04-S081, P04-S084, P04-S017.

P04-AP10.text: - P04-AP10 — The minute candles used: the monitor applies no as-of truncation or completeness test, so a still-forming minute (if the broker sent one) enters the fold and can cause an immediate, irreversible confirmation or rejection; and its filter by the divert time excludes the divert's own minute under the start-of-minute reading of the label and includes it under the end reading; no source states which was intended (A05 HA-03, HA-04; history questions A05-17 and A05-29 OPEN). For comparison, A18's PB-01 stage states "only CLOSED 5-min candles are ever evaluated (`truncate_to_asof` drops a still-forming bar)" (`v3_chain/pb01_entry.py` L20 to L21). Sources: P04-S066 to P04-S068, P04-S142.

P04-AP11.text: - P04-AP11 — The direction is tested in different forms along the path: case-insensitive and stripped in `evaluate` (`_is_long`), exact in the audit row (L399) and in the resumption (`signals/signal_processor.py` L2435), and through the side in the diverter (L321 to L322); they agree for the two values the strategy schema admits and would disagree for any other stored value. Sources: P04-S018, P04-S105, P04-S111.

P04-AP12.text: - P04-AP12 — The monitor's rejection statuses are outside the `REJECTED*` family: `RETEST_REJECTED_TIMEOUT`, `_BREAK_DOWN` and `_RECLAIM_UP` begin with `RETEST_`, so the dashboard funnel counts them as "accepted", the signal-status report as "other", and the end-of-day prune never takes them, while the divert's own `REJECTED_RETEST_DUP` and the resumption's `REJECTED_RETEST_BAD_STRUCTURE` are "rejected" and prunable (the readers' logic is their owners'). Sources: P04-S060, P04-S059, P04-S057, P04-S103.

P04-AP13.text: - P04-AP13 — The boot order (A01 C13's A08 side; C13 unchanged): the monitor's thread starts at `main.py` L3797, before the startup reconcile that, by its comment, "MUST precede" any sizing or placement (L3869 to L3879) and before the processor's start; by the code's structure a rehydrated candidate could be resumed on the monitor's thread from its first poll, 20 s after start; at the committed wiring the evaluation raises before any callback (P04-AP01). Sources: P04-S092, P04-S151.

P04-AP14.text: - P04-AP14 — Partial wiring after a failure in the V2 block (A01 C37's A08 side; C37 unchanged): the diverter and the square-off's reference are bound before the starts, and the `except` resets only `retest_monitor`, so a failed thread start can leave diverts parking candidates in a monitor that never polls, with `_shutdown` unaware of it. Sources: P04-S091, P04-S152.

P04-AP15.text: - P04-AP15 — Bookkeeping failures that the caller does not see: a failed `retest_state` insert leaves a memory-only parking that the diverter cannot detect and a restart loses (`register` "Never raises"); a failed `RETEST_WAITING` write leaves a parked candidate whose signal shows `PASSED` and has no divert row; `clear_all` reports the in-memory count, not the rows deleted; `stop` resets `_worker` even when its join timed out. (c) Zerodha support article "Why does the Open, High, Low, Close (OHLC) of historical data on the Kite charts sometimes not match the records updated in NSE or BSE?", `https://support.zerodha.com/category/trading-and-markets/kite-web-and-mobile/charts/articles/kite-charts-not-matching-as-per-the-records-in-nse-or-bse` (no date shown): "Zerodha adjusts the data for corporate actions"; "Kite modifies historical OHLC data to account for corporate actions", listing bonus issues, stock splits, rights issues, spin-offs and extraordinary dividends; the article speaks of the Kite charts, not of the API. (d) Kite Connect developer forum (the broker's forum; not documentation): thread "documentation of adjustments in historical data", `https://kite.trade/forum/discussion/15358/documentation-of-adjustments-in-historical-data` (July 2025), and thread "Historical 5-minute API data: corporate-action price and volume adjustments", `https://kite.trade/forum/discussion/16280/historical-5-minute-api-data-corporate-action-price-and-volume-adjustments` (posts dated 28 September to 1 October, year not shown): the replies in both threads come from one forum account, whose role the pages do not show (no staff or moderator mark). The July 2025 reply states "We adjust historical data for corporate actions to improve analysis" and that the adjustments cover bonuses, splits, rights issues, spin-offs and extraordinary dividends; the replies of 29 September and 1 October state "We do adjust historical data for corporate actions to improve analysis", the same list with extraordinary dividends "(more than 2%)", that the adjustments "are applied during the beginning-of-day process on the ex-date (before market open)", that "Kite Connect does not provide an unadjusted historical price-and-volume series", that "Historical candle values will be updated from time to time due to subsequent corporate-action adjustments", and that volume "will also be adjusted ... except dividends". Forum replies are not documentation and carry less weight than sources (a) and (b). The July 2025 question asked for the historical-data documentation to state the adjustments; source (a), read on 26-Nov-2026, does not state them.

P05-S030.label: FACT and INTERPRETATION
P05-S030.text: - P05-S030 FACT and INTERPRETATION (the loop, L80 to L89): FACT: `worst_ratio = 1.0`, `worst_when = None`, `prev = rows[0]`; for each following row `c`, when `prev["close"]` is truthy, `ratio = c["close"] / prev["close"]`, and the ratio replaces `worst_ratio` (with `worst_when = (prev["date"], c["date"])`) only when `abs(ratio - 1.0) > abs(worst_ratio - 1.0)`; `prev = c` after every row. P06-S009.text: - P06-S009 FACT (the model and its place; A02's files, interface): `SystemConfig.sr_detector: SRDetectorConfig = Field(default_factory=SRDetectorConfig)` (`core/config_loader.py` L2012) and `SystemConfig.structure_exit: StructureExitConfig = Field(default_factory=StructureExitConfig)` (L2017), so either section may be absent from the file and is then built from its field defaults. `SRDetectorConfig` (L1153 to L1255) has `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (L1162), 45 fields, every one with a default (L1163 to L1223), and three validators: `anchor_intraday_interval` in {`5minute`, `15minute`, `30minute`} (L1225 to L1234), `require_confidence` in {`HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`} (L1236 to L1241) and `timeframes` non-empty and within {`day`, `60minute`, `30minute`, `15minute`, `5minute`} (L1243 to L1255). No field has a range or sign validator (as P01-S055, P03-S025 and P04-S019 record for their keys). The committed block (`config/system_config.yaml` L508 to L545) sets 34 of the 45 fields; the 11 others take the loader default (P06-S057). `StructureExitConfig` (L1577 to L1607) has `extra="forbid"` (L1587), six fields with defaults (L1588 to L1593) and validators for `min_zone_confidence` and `break_strong_close_frac` only (L1595 to L1607); `structure_exit_enabled: bool = False` (L1588) has none.

The same holds for an exception that leaves `_main_locked` after L3504 (passing the same `finally`; handled at L4288 to L4293, exit 1 for a `TradingSystemError`, exit 2 otherwise), for example the re-raised `EffectCompositionError` at L4246 (a `RuntimeError` subclass, `core/effect_telemetry.py` L71, so exit 2). INTERPRETATION: at that point no placement has happened, so the detector's queue is empty (P03-S036); the monitor's first poll may or may not have come, depending on the elapsed time (UNKNOWN / NOT ESTABLISHED, P06-U03).

P06-S086.label: INTERPRETATION
P06-S086.text: - P06-S086 INTERPRETATION (what the order means for the A08 objects, from P06-S085 and the parts): (a) the processor is stopped before the detector, so no new candidate is offered while the detector drains (the comment's stated reason; what `signal_proc.stop()` waits for is A06's); (b) the monitor is stopped before the structure exit and the warmer, and the warmer last of the three; the zone cache's two readers (P02-S097), the diverter (called only on the processor's workers, stopped at L1689 to L1692) and the structure exit (L1737 to L1741), are stopped before the warmer that fills the cache; the monitor reads neither the warmer nor the cache; (c) each A08 `stop` joins its worker for 2.0 s without checking the outcome and does not interrupt a worker inside a fetch, so a fetch in progress can finish after its `stop` returned (P03-S031, P03-S033; P02-S088, P02-S089; P04-S089, P04-S090); the shutdown event set at L1629 makes the limiter abort waits (P02-S089); (d) every A08 stop precedes `candle_store.stop()` and `store.close()`, so a worker that finishes its last item within its join finds the store open; a worker that outlives its join can reach `store.close()` (L1828) still running (the detector's write, P03-S033; the monitor's release or callback, P04-S090). The diverter and the zone cache have nothing to stop (P06-S077). A01 C18 records the shutdown's total duration, A01's (unchanged).
